447: Built around Huron Blackheart, Abaddon, a swarm of Chosen, Cultist Mobs, and Defilers, this is a mass-horde gunline that layers elite shock troops over a tide of expendable bodies, running Cabal of Chaos with Fellhammer Siege-Host in the vast majority of lists to make the whole army dramatically harder to wound with strength-over-toughness attacks. The plan is to flood objectives with cultists and Chosen while Defilers and Dark Pact-fueled psyker shooting grind out damage, with Huron and Masters of the Maelstrom generating the command economy to keep everything moving. It punishes ranged-heavy armies brutally — Fellhammer's wound-roll penalty turns many high-strength shooting phases into near-misses against what should be soft targets. Melee alpha-strike armies that bypass the wound modifier and get into the cultist screen early can collapse the objective base before the elite core can respond.
448:
Built around Defilers, Venomcrawlers, and Vashtorr the Arkifane supported by Warpsmiths and Cultist screens, this list runs dual detachments — Cabal of Chaos primary and Soulforged Warpack secondary — to supercharge its Daemon Vehicles through Dark Pacts, granting +1 to Wound on ranged attacks and +2 Attacks in melee whenever they invoke their contracts.

The engine is Vashtorr enabling and buffing the Daemon Vehicle core while Warpsmiths keep them operational; the list scores by smashing through mid-board with heavily buffed Defilers and Venomcrawlers that threaten both armour and infantry simultaneously. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't absorb the sheer volume of boosted Daemon Vehicle attacks across multiple phases. Aggressive horde or cheap screen-heavy lists that can clog the mid-board and dilute Dark Pact activations, combined with anything applying consistent mortal wounds at range, expose how fragile the activation chain becomes when vehicles die early.
450: Built around Lady Malys, Drazhar, Lelith Hesperax, Incubi, and Wyches swarming out of Venoms and Raiders, this is an Exhibition of Slaughter and Skysplinter Assault double-detachment list that weaponizes its transports as delivery systems — every disembark turn grants melee weapons Lance and ranged weapons Ignores Cover, while Wych Cult melee attacks carry Lethal Hits against anything that isn't a Monster or Vehicle. The gameplan is to flood the midboard with throwaway Wych screens, then surge named characters and Incubi out of transports directly into priority threats, stacking Lance on the charge to punch through high-save targets. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally — the sheer volume of Lethal Hit melee attacks overwhelms damage-efficient infantry that can't afford to trade bodies. Armies that can deep-strike denial or shoot the transports off the board before disembark turn collapse the entire engine, since stranded infantry lose both their delivery mechanism and the critical Skysplinter buffs.
466: Built around Flawless Blades, Infractors, Lord Exultants, Defilers, Tormentors, Winged Daemon Princes, Lucius the Eternal, Noise Marines, and Fulgrim, this is a transported infantry brawler that floods the midboard with melee threats delivered in Rhinos and supported by heavy daemon engine firepower. The Coterie of the Conceited detachment forces a pledge each round — correctly predicting how many enemy units you'll destroy generates Pact points, so the entire game plan is built around engineering reliable kill counts rather than simply brawling blindly. It punishes army designs that spread out into small units, since more enemy models means more pledgeable kills and a bigger Pact point engine. Armies that deny engagement — heavy screening, castle gunlines that force you to overextend for kills — will cause failed pledges and starve you of resources before you can dictate terms.
473: Built around Paladin Squads, Brotherhood Terminator Squads, Grand Master Voldus, Brotherhood Chaplains, and supporting Strike and Interceptor Squads, this list runs the Argent Assault detachment to ensure Paladins wound up even when punching into high-Toughness targets. The win condition is layered melee pressure across multiple fronts — Paladins grind through elite infantry and monsters while Terminators, frequently supplemented by Hallowed Conclave's Fell Back and fight/shoot ability, contest and reclaim objectives without surrendering board presence after a bad combat. It punishes slow, durable armies that rely on Toughness to survive melee, since the core detachment strips that defensive buffer from Paladins entirely, and the mobile toolkit of Interceptors keeps the pressure spread wide. However, high-volume shooting lists that can strip Paladins before they engage, or armies that deny the melee phase through layered screens, crack this build open by neutering the wound-roll engine before it fires.
481: Built around the Knight Castellan, this list plants one of the game's most punishing heavy platforms at its center and surrounds it with a flexible supporting cast of Dominus walkers, Armigers, and occasional Cerastus Knights. The Dominus Foebreakers detachment's +1 to hit rolls against units in terrain areas means the Castellan and its kin are actively rewarded for targeting enemies sheltering behind cover, punishing the screen-and-deny defensive postures that most armies rely on. Archeotech Autoloaders amplifies this engine further, and Gate Warden Lance's defensive-line mechanic in nearly three-quarters of lists gives the build a structural objective anchor that lets it trade efficiently while holding ground. It struggles against highly mobile, low-footprint armies that can deny terrain exposure and contest objectives without clustering, robbing the +1 hit bonus of its targets and forcing the Knights into inefficient shooting.
480: Built around Armiger Warglaives, Armiger Helverins, and a Knight Castellan, this is a mobile anti-armour hammer that floods the board with fast, durable chassis across every threat range. The win condition is layered firepower — Warglaives close and shred vehicles in melee while Helverins suppress at range, with the Castellan's massed heavy weapons punishing anything that clusters or sits static. Where detachment rules apply, Spearhead-At-Arms multiplies Bondsman activations across up to three Armigers simultaneously, dramatically spiking output on key turns. It punishes low-model-count elite armies and mechanised lists through anti-armour overload, but struggles against high-volume screening and armies that can reliably degrade its expensive chassis before it can leverage that compounding firepower.
430: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Hekaton Land Fortresses, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and Kâhl, this list runs the Hearthguard Covenant detachment, flooding midboard with tough, short-range elite infantry and heavy fire support vehicles backed by fast-moving Hernkyn Pioneers and Sagitaurs screening the advance. The win condition is closing distance to trigger the detachment's re-roll wound rolls of 1 inside 9", then unleashing massed Thunderkyn and Hearthguard volleys to grind through durable targets while Kapricus Carriers and Yaegirs lock down secondaries. It punishes slow, low-mobility armies that cannot keep elite units out of that 9" kill zone, where the wound re-roll advantage compounds across multiple high-volume shooting units simultaneously. It cracks open against fast alpha-strike lists that can surgically delete the Hearthguard before they close range, neutering the core wound-reroll engine before it ever fires.
482: Built around Armiger Warglaives, a Knight Castellan, a Knight Crusader, Cerastus Knight Lancers, and Armiger Helverins, this Freeblade Company list fields an independent warband of mixed Knights with no House allegiance — every model benefits from Feel No Pain 6+ and regenerates 1 wound per Command phase, giving the whole army sustained durability across a long game. The win condition is layered anti-armour pressure: the Castellan and Crusader dump overwhelming firepower into hard targets while Lancers and Warglaives close in for melee kills, with Hunter's Eye and Mysterious Guardian enhancements sharpening accuracy and survivability on key pieces. It punishes armies built around elite vehicle or monster spam that can't sustain attrition against a self-healing, multi-threat battleline. It cracks under coordinated high-volume damage or anti-tank overload that races ahead of the per-phase wound recovery before the Knights can reach scoring positions.
456: Built around Canoptek Wraiths, Technomancers, Canoptek Reanimators, Illuminor Szeras, Ophydian Destroyers, Skorpekh Lord, the Void Dragon, and the Nightbringer, this Awakened Dynasty list pairs near-unkillable melee threats with a robust self-repair engine. The plan is to crash durable, hard-to-remove units into mid-board objectives while Reanimators and Technomancers cycle wounds back, grinding opponents into attrition losses while C'tan anchor flanks and Ophydians punish overextension. Awakened Dynasty's +1 to Hit for CHARACTER-led units turns already-threatening melee squads into efficient kill chains, punishing low-wound elite armies that can't trade effectively against regenerating bodies. Lists that flood the board with cheap screens or deliver high-volume mortal wounds bypass the reanimation loop entirely, starving the engine of the time it needs to grind.
486: Built around nearly five squads of Boyz backed by multiple Painboys, Warbosses, Bigbosses, Ghazghkull Thraka, and Wazdakka Gutsmek under the Green Tide detachment, this is a wall-of-green mid-board brawler that floods every lane with bodies. The plan is to keep Boyz blobs at ten-plus models to trigger their 5+ invulnerable save, stack Painboy healing to deny attrition, and crash multiple buffed mobs into the enemy simultaneously to overwhelm combat on every objective at once. It punishes elite low-volume lists brutally — when your opponent can't generate enough attacks to chew through 5+ invulnerable, feel-no-pain-adjacent Boyz, the weight of bodies simply grinds them off the table. Boards against high-volume mortal wounds or mass AP-agnostic shooting that can kill models faster than Painboys can patch them, cracking the critical ten-model threshold and collapsing that invulnerable save.
487: Built around Mozrog Skragbad, multiple Beastbosses on Squigosaurs, Squighog Boyz, Kill Rigs, Beast Snagga Boyz, and Gretchin screens, this is a pure Beast Snagga brawler running Da Big Hunt with Rollin' Deff in roughly two-thirds of lists to give Kill Rigs guaranteed 6" advances and charge re-rolls. The engine is Da Big Hunt's Prey designation: every turn a high-value enemy MONSTER, VEHICLE, or CHARACTER is tagged, and the entire Beast Snagga mass — Squighogs, Beastbosses, and Boyz alike — funnels charge re-rolls into deleting it while Kill Rigs slam home alongside them. It punishes elite armoured lists by overwhelming anti-tank targets one at a time with layered charge reliability and sheer mobile hitting power across multiple threats simultaneously. Armies that can screen out charges, thin the squighog packages at range before contact, or exploit the minimal shooting output will crack it open before the Prey engine pays off.
468: Built around Vulkan He'stan, multiple Infernus Squads, Librarians, Land Raider Redeemers, Bladeguard Veterans, Adrax Agatone, Scout Squads, and Sternguard Veterans, this Forgefather's Seekers list plays a close-range fire-superiority game where every ranged weapon gains Assault and punches harder at 12" or less. The engine is He'stan unlocking Infernus Squads to act after disembarking from Redeemers, flooding mid-board objectives with high-volume flamer and melta output while Librarians cycle Psychic Disciplines — most often Divination for re-rolls or Pyromancy for additional punch — to amplify each kill chain. It absolutely punishes infantry-heavy and light-vehicle lists that are forced to cluster in mid-board ranges, where the Strength bonus and transport delivery create an overwhelming volume of short-range fire. Armies that can stay beyond 12", strip the Redeemers early with dedicated anti-tank overload, or deny mid-board positioning crack the list open before the close-range engine ever comes online.
488: Built around multiple Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Lootas, Flash Gitz, Tankbustas, and Big Mek Dakkarigsall operating under Dread Mob's randomised (or chosen) weapon ability table, with Gretchin hordes and Trukks providing a cheap, mobile screen-and-transport backbone. The plan is to park an overwhelming volume of variable-but-buffable firepower mid-board, leverage Dread Mob's ability selection on key activations for reliable lethal output, then use Wazdakka and Trukk-mounted Tankbustas to threaten armour from unexpected angles. It punishes static elite gunlines and low-model-count armies that cannot contest mid-board presence against this volume of bodies and shots. Armies that can strip the Gretchin screen early with blast weapons or alpha-strike the Shokk Attack Guns before Dread Mob triggers collapse the engine fast, since the gunline lacks durable defensive depth once its cheap screening horde is gone.
467: Built around Marneus Calgar, Victrix Honour Guard, Ballistus Dreadnoughts, Repulsor Executioners, and a screen of Scouts and Intercessors, this is a gunline-heavy Blade of Ultramar list that weaponises Calgar's unique ability to recycle Combat Doctrines, cycling the same doctrine more than once per game to keep optimal buffs active across multiple turns. The win condition is sustained mid-to-long range firepower from stacked Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus Dreadnoughts, with Jump Pack Assault Intercessors threatening flanks and contested objectives to force opponents off scoring positions. It punishes slow, low-mobility armies that cannot contest the midfield early, as the gunline gets free reign to delete threats while cheap Scouts and Intercessors bank primary points. Fast alpha-strike armies or those with deep strike pressure crack it open by forcing the gunline to react before Calgar's doctrine engine fully pays off.
428: Built around Riptides, Broadsides, The Twin Lance, Ghostkeels, and Stealth Battlesuits screening for them, with Pathfinders and Piranhas providing mobile forward presence, this is a Mont'ka gunline that moves and shoots without penalty across the first three rounds. The win condition is layering Guided [LETHAL HITS] onto high-volume anti-armour platforms — Riptides and Broadsides converting hits into wounds far above average — while Pathfinders lock down Markerlight targets and Piranhas threaten flanks and contest secondaries. It punishes slow, armour-heavy lists that cannot hide from a shooting army that suffers no movement penalty and generates lethal hits on guided units turn after turn. It cracks under pressure from aggressive melee armies or deep-strike threats that can collapse the Pathfinder screen before the Lethal Hits engine fully activates.
483: Built around Biovores, Neurolictors, Neurotyrants, Lictors, Genestealers, and Norn Emissaries, this is a high-mobility infiltration swarm that floods the board with synapse-linked hunter organisms arriving from unexpected angles. The plan is to choke out opponent scoring through pervasive board presence — Neurolictors and Lictors suppress enemy actions and deny safe positioning while Genestealers and Norn Emissaries punish anything caught in the open, with Biovores applying persistent chip pressure from safety. It excels against slower, static gunlines that cannot reposition fast enough to escape the encirclement, turning their inability to screen every threat vector into a tempo collapse. Lists that can alpha-strike the infiltrating screens before they establish position, or that bring enough board-wide threat to punish the relatively thin defensive layers, will crack this open before the stranglehold sets in.
490: Built around Sekhetar Robots, Defilers, Forgefiends, Tzaangor Shamans, and Exalted Sorcerers on Discs, this is a psyker-empowered daemon-engine gunline running the Sekhetar Cohort and Warpforged Cabal detachments. The engine is Psyker auras stacked on top of daemon machines: Shamans and Sorcerers push +1 WS onto the Robots in melee while keeping Vehicles within 6" to fish re-rolls on hit, wound, and damage, letting the Forgefiends and Defilers pump out consistent high-volume, high-quality fire across multiple phases. It punishes slower armour-heavy lists that can't contest mid-table, where Robots with Psychic-tagged melee attacks and re-roll-supported Vehicles grind through tough targets efficiently. Armies that can alpha-strike the Psyker bubble before it activates, or flood the board with cheap screens to block aura ranges, will crack the support network and leave the daemon engines underperforming.
489: Built around Sekhetar Robots buffed by Sorcerers in Terminator Armour and Sorcerers on foot, backed by Scarab Occult Terminators, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, Rubric Marines, Tzaangors, Daemon Princes with Wings, and Magnus the Red under the Hexwarp Thrallband and Sekhetar Cohort detachments. The plan is to saturate the mid-board early enough to trigger Hexwarp Thrallband's No Man's Land Flow of Magic, then use Sekhetar Cohort's Infusion aura to pump the Robots' melee WS while their attacks gain the Psychic keyword, creating a layered kill chain of massed Psychic ranged fire from Enlightened and screens, followed by supercharged Robot melee threats. The sheer volume of bodies and overlapping Psychic synergies punishes lower-model-count elite armies that cannot out-trade the horde's efficiency across multiple phases. The build cracks under focused alpha-strike pressure targeting the Sorcerer bubbles before Infusion activates, collapsing the Robots' melee output and leaving an expensive horde without its damage multiplier.
427: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinder Teams, a deep roster of Crisis variants (Starscythe, Fireknife, Sunforge), Riptides, Ghostkeels, Coldstar and Enforcer Commanders, and Commander Farsight, this list exploits the Advanced Acquisition Cadre's core rule to keep Stealth Battlesuits and Pathfinders hidden even after shooting — locking in persistent marker support and board presence simultaneously. The win condition is layered anti-armour pressure: Retaliation Cadre (72% of lists) sharpens Crisis Battlesuits inside 12" to Strength+1 and AP+1 inside 8", letting the kill chain strip vehicles and elite infantry through close-range volley fire while fast Coldstars reposition to pick angles. It punishes heavy-armour lists badly, overloading save rolls with high-volume, high-AP battlesuit fire that most transport-heavy armies cannot screen against efficiently. It struggles against swarm lists that flood objectives and deny clean sight lines, and against opponents who can force engagement outside 8" where the Retaliation Cadre's AP bonus disappears.
484: Built around Norn Assimilators, Norn Emissaries, Biovores, Pyrovores, Psychophages, and Ripper Swarms, this is a durable mid-board pressure machine running the Assimilation Swarm detachment, where HARVESTER units regenerate wounds and return destroyed Infantry models every Command phase to keep the swarm perpetually topped up. The win condition is sustained attrition — grind opponents out of scoring positions by making key units nearly impossible to fully remove, while Biovores chip screening units and Pyrovores punish clumped Infantry with board-wide threat. It punishes lists that rely on concentrated burst damage to remove threats, since anything that survives a shooting phase can regenerate back to fighting strength before the opponent gets another shot. Anti-regeneration lists that can reliably delete entire units in a single activation — rather than wounding across several — expose the fundamental fragility of the mechanism, as a model returned from nothing still needs wounds restored the following turn.
518: Built around Lokhust Destroyers, Lokhust Lords, Ophydian Destroyers, Skorpekh Destroyers, Skorpekh Lords, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, Lychguard, a C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, and the unique character Nekrosor Ammentar, this list runs Cursed Legion to pump Destroyer Cult weapon Strength by +2 baseline — and by a further +2 after the first kill or half-strength trigger each turn, creating a snowballing damage chain. The plan is to open a crack in the opponent's army with ranged Lokhust fire, trip the strength escalation, then crash Ophydian and Skorpekh units into whatever survives to clear objectives and score through attrition. It punishes mid-density armies — those that cluster models into killable clumps — because every destroyed or half-strength unit accelerates the weapon Strength spiral, making each subsequent fight hit harder. Spread-out, durable elite lists that can absorb the first kill without crumbling deny the escalation trigger and let the opponent fight back before the chain ever reaches peak output.
517: Built around nearly two Doomsday Arks, the Silent King, Technomancers, Canoptek Wraiths, Flayed Ones, and Ophydian Destroyers, this Starshatter Arsenal list blends hard-hitting vehicle firepower with a versatile, multi-threat melee and denial package. The engine is the detachment's hit bonus on objective-contested targets — Doomsday Arks and the Silent King hammer whatever sits on or near objectives, while Wraiths, Flayed Ones, and Ophydian Destroyers flood in to contest, harass, and kill in melee, generating scoring opportunities across the board. It punishes static gunline armies that cluster on objectives, turning their defensive positioning into a free accuracy bonus against them. Highly mobile elite armies that can flood and isolate individual threats crack it open, since the reanimation support is inconsistent and the list lacks the raw defensive depth to absorb coordinated alpha strikes across multiple flanks simultaneously.
530: Built around Allarus Custodians, Vertus Praetors, Dawneagle Shield-Captains, Allarus Shield-Captains, Blade Champions, Witchseekers, Custodian Guard, and Custodian Wardens, this Lions of the Emperor list weaponises deliberate isolation — every non-Vehicle unit that fights or shoots without a friendly model within 6" gains +1 to Hit and +1 to Wound, incentivising a spread-out, aggressive deployment across the entire board. The plan is to push fast with jetbike Captains and Vertus Praetors into mid-table, then crack open objectives through superior individual combat output, with Allarus Custodians providing deep-strike threat to punish over-commitment and score secondaries. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies hardest — when the opponent can't screen wide enough to deny the isolation bonus, each Custodian unit effectively fights a tier above its points cost. Dense horde screens or armies that can flood the 6" bubble force units to clump, collapsing the hit-and-wound bonus and exposing the build's relatively low model count to attrition it cannot replace.
525: Built around Land Speeder Vengeances, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, Land Speeders, Ravenwing Black Knights, Outrider Squads, Ravenwing Command Squads, and Sammael, this is a Company of Hunters / Darkflight Pursuit force that floods the table with fast-moving skimmers and bikes. The engine is relentless pressure: Assault on all ranged weapons means every unit shoots after advancing or falling back, letting Speeders and bikes contest objectives while maintaining full firepower, while Ignores Cover on RAVENWING FLY units strips defensive bonuses from anything trying to hide. It punishes gunline armies and anything static — the ability to advance-and-shoot or fall-back-and-shoot across a wall of skimmers overwhelms lists that rely on positional trading and cover saves. Highly mobile elite infantry or deep-striking threats can crack it open, since the relatively fragile chassis become costly to protect when opponents can appear inside the screen or force unfavorable combats the bikes can't efficiently exit.
529: Built around Grey Hunters, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Wolf Guard Battle Leaders, Wolf Scouts, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Ragnar Blackmane, Blood Claws, and Wolf Priests operating under Saga of the Beastslayer, this is a transport-heavy infantry swarm that floods the board with bodies capable of splitting Grey Hunter squads mid-deployment to contest multiple zones simultaneously. The win condition is built on Lethal Hits triggering against every Character, Monster, and Vehicle in the opponent's army, letting mid-table brawlers punch well above their weight into armoured targets while Grey Hunters perform actions without surrendering their shooting via Veterans of the Fang. It punishes elite low-model-count lists by overwhelming them with multi-unit pressure and mobile anti-armour that makes expensive vehicles uncomfortable to expose. Horde armies and high-volume mortal-wound output crack it open by drowning the infantry screen before the Saga kill-chain can activate at scale.
521: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Ghostkeel Battlesuits, Vespid Stingwings, Pathfinders, multiple Crisis suit variants, Riptides, Broadsides, Commander Farsight, and Coldstar Commanders, this is a wide T'au force blending alien auxiliaries with a full battlesuit roster across a mix of detachment packages. The plan is to layer Pathfinder spotting onto a deep anti-armour kill chain — Sunforge and Starscythe Crisis suits, Riptides, and Broadsides flood the board with high-strength shooting while Stealth and Ghostkeel units hold mid-table under their Localised Stealth Projectors aura, contesting objectives behind a screen of Vespid and Kroot bodies with Harnessed Alien Instincts. It punishes armour-heavy lists through sheer anti-tank overload, stacking mobile platforms that can reposition and fire from multiple angles simultaneously. Aggressive alpha-strike armies that can crack the mid-table stealth bubble early expose how fragile the individual units are once the screening layer collapses.
441:
Built around Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, multiple Librarians in Terminator armour, Azrael, and Sternguard Veterans, this is a Librarius Conclave psychic-amplified terminator hammer with a dense infantry core of Scouts and Intercessors holding the map underneath it.

The plan is to flex Biomancy, Divination, or Pyromancy across the entire psyker roster each round, routing that battlefield-wide buff into the Knights and Companions to make the close-range kill package hit harder, move faster, or chew through whatever the matchup demands, while Sternguard provide mid-range firepower and objective bodies generate steady secondary pressure.

It punishes lists that can't withstand elite multi-wound melee, as the Knights and Companions swamp anti-horde armies and ignore volume-of-fire attrition through natural durability.

Fragile to dedicated anti-tank overload and fast-moving screens that block the advance lane, since the melee core is relatively slow without Biomancy up and loses tempo badly if the Librarians are neutralised early.
550: Built around multiple Lords of Change, Kairos Fateweaver, Be'lakor, and Screamers as fast objective contesters, with Flamers providing concentrated short-range firepower, this list runs Lords Of The Warp paired with Scintillating Legion to layer re-rolls through Flux tokens across its Tzeentch core. The win condition is relentless mobile pressure — Screamers skate across the board denying opponent scoring while Lords of Change and Kairos stack layered threat vectors that force impossible target-priority decisions, with Flux tokens ensuring the critical hit or wound roll lands when it matters. It punishes slower, high-toughness armies through mobile anti-armour overload, hitting from multiple angles simultaneously so no single defensive screen can contain it. Armies that can strip its characters early — particularly those with long-range precision or alpha-strike deep strike — crack it open by eliminating the Tzeentch monsters that the re-roll economy is built around.
551:
Built around Skarbrand, multiple Bloodletter bricks, Bloodcrushers, Flesh Hounds, Rendmasters on Blood Thrones, and a Bloodthirster, this is a wall-to-wall Khorne assault list that drowns the board in bodies and murder.

The Blood Legion detachment's surge move mechanic is the engine: every time an enemy unit moves within 8" of a Khorne daemon, your units lurch forward reactively, collapsing the gap and forcing combat on your terms while Bloodletters and Bloodcrushers pile in to grind opponents off objectives.

Nurglings and Plaguebearers screen and deny your key pieces from deep-strike disruption, freeing Skarbrand and the Bloodthirster to hunt elite and monster-heavy lists that can't absorb the volume of high-lethality melee attacks this army generates.

Shooting armies that dictate range and movement — particularly those that can kite, castle, or alpha-strike key pieces before the surge kicks in — can crack this open before the kill chain ever closes.
459: Built around Rogal Dorn Commanders, Scout Sentinels, Hellhounds, Leman Russ Vanquishers, Leman Russ Battle Tanks, Rogal Dorn Battle Tanks, and Tech-Priest Enginseers, this is a heavy armoured gunline that uses Scout Sentinels' Signal Flares ability — granted by the Designation Force detachment — to paint targets for massed battle-tank firepower. The plan is to advance Scout Sentinels aggressively into forward positions, light up priority threats with Signal Flares, and delete them with concentrated long-range shooting from multiple Leman Russ and Dorn chassis while Enginseers keep the armour operational. It punishes mid-table elite armies that lack the volume to clear both the forward Sentinel screen and the tank line behind it, overwhelming single-wound-removal tools with sheer armoured mass. However, it folds to fast alpha-strike lists that can crash into the tank line early, since the Squadron and Titanic units have limited recourse once enemies lock them in Engagement Range before Signal Flares can activate.
465: Built around daemonettes, defilers, lords exultant, infractors, tormentors, noise marines, and rhino-delivered infantry, this is a mid-table brawler that floods the board with Legions of Excess and Emperor's Children units to keep as many models as possible Empowered — granting Sustained Hits across the force. The plan is to crash a mass of Empowered bodies into the mid-board early, generate overwhelming volume of attacks through Sustained Hits triggers, and grind opponents off objectives through sheer attrition rather than surgical strikes. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot absorb the cascading output from multiple Empowered hordes hitting simultaneously across several objectives. It cracks open against armies that can isolate and delete individual units before they cluster into Empowered range, breaking the mutual-buff engine before it fires.
546: Built around the Void Dragon, Nightbringer, Deceiver, and multiple Transcendent C'tan alongside Flayed Ones and Hexmark Destroyers, this is a monster-mash battleline running Hand Of The Dynasty so its Immortals and Warriors advance-and-act while the C'tan do the heavy lifting. The win condition is controlling board space with unkillable monsters that threaten every angle simultaneously, using the C'tan's raw durability and threat saturation to force bad trades while objective-holders screen and score. It punishes attrition-focused armies that cannot generate enough high-quality anti-monster shooting to neutralise multiple T10+ threats in a single turn. It cracks when faced with alpha-strike lists that can delete one or two C'tan immediately, collapsing the threat-saturation equation before the Flayed Ones and Hexmarks can punish the overextension.
544: Built around multiple Skorpekh Lord-led Skorpekh Destroyer units, the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, Nekrosor Ammentar, Illuminor Szeras, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers under Lokhust Lords, the Silent King, and Ophydian Destroyers, this Awakened Dynasty list weaponizes the detachment's +1 to Hit across nearly every combat and shooting unit on the table. The win condition is layered threat saturation — Ophydians and Skorpekhs hunt infantry midboard while Lokhust Heavy Destroyers and the Void Dragon crack vehicles, with Enaegic Dermal Bond keeping lead characters alive long enough to cycle damage into scoring turns. It punishes lists with spread-out, mid-toughness targets that can't absorb simultaneous melee and heavy anti-armour pressure from multiple angles. Concentrated alpha-strike armies or elite high-damage output can strip the attached characters before the hit-bonus engine fires, unraveling the whole threat package.
526: Built around Lokhust Destroyers, Nekrosor Ammentar, Ophydian Destroyers, Lokhust Lords, the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, Lychguard, and the Overlord with Translocation Shroud, this is a multi-vector Necron murder machine that floods the board with fast, durable threat vectors across multiple phases. The plan is to overwhelm opponents by projecting lethal ranged pressure through Lokhust Destroyers and the Void Dragon while Ophydian Destroyers threaten sudden melee eruptions from unexpected angles, forcing opponents to defend multiple kill zones simultaneously rather than concentrating resources. Its high mobility toolkit punishes slower, static gunlines that can't reposition quickly enough to address threats from all directions at once. It cracks open against tight alpha-strike armies and anything capable of stripping the Lokhust Destroyers before they activate, since losing that ranged backbone early collapses the layered threat structure the entire plan depends on.
556: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, massed Boyz, Beast Snagga Boyz, Squighog Boyz, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Mozrog Skragbad, and supporting Beastbosses, this is a War Horde wall of green that hits every melee phase with Sustained Hits 1 across the entire roster. The plan is pure mid-board collision: flood objectives with disposable Gretchin screens, deliver elite beat-sticks in Trukks, and grind opposing units into paste through sheer volume of sustained melee attacks while Painboys keep key pieces alive. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot absorb the raw number of incoming attacks or contest multiple points simultaneously. It cracks against high-volume shooting lists and fast deep-strike threats that can isolate and delete priority pieces before the green tide reaches combat range.
558: Built around Wazdakka Gutsmek, massed Warbikers, Deffkoptas, Deffkilla Wartrikes, and Boyz screened by Gretchin, this is a wave of fast, hard-hitting Orks running primarily Kult of Speed — letting Speed Freeks shoot and charge after Advancing or Falling Back. The plan is to flood mid-table turn one, use Advance-and-charge to crash into multiple units simultaneously, and grind through brawls while Gretchin sit objectives behind the carnage. It punishes slower, lower-model-count armies that can't handle simultaneous threats across the entire front — the sheer volume of bodies and bikes forces attrition trades that favor Orks. Anything with high-volume mortal wounds, strong overwatch, or elite deep-striking units that can surgically remove the Deffkoptas and Wartrikes before they engage will crack the momentum early.
533: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Crisis Sunforge and Starscythe Battlesuits, Coldstar Commanders, The Twin Lance, Pathfinders, Vespid Stingwings, and Kroot Carnivores operating under Experimental Prototype Cadre — which extends Battlesuit Character ranged threat by 6" — this list plays a highly mobile, multi-vector shooting army that punishes opponents for clustering or castling. The win condition is a coordinated kill chain: Pathfinders spot priority targets, Coldstar Commanders and Crisis suits delete them at extended range, while Vespid and Kroot flood midboard objectives to generate secondary pressure. It punishes slow or mechanized lists that rely on staying outside threat range, since extended Battlesuit Character reach collapses that safety buffer entirely. It cracks when faced with fast melee threats or elite deep-strike pressure that can bypass the midboard screen before Pathfinders can establish consistent Guided-unit chains.
561: Built around Scarab Occult Terminators buffed by Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, Sekhetar Robots, Tzaangors as screening chaff, Ahriman, and a Daemon Prince of Tzeentch, this list plays the Rubricae Phalanx detachment, whose core rule grants Rubricae models an armour save bonus against any attack with an unmodified Damage characteristic of 1. The plan is to march an elite, damage-resistant brick into the midboard, use Tzaangor screens and ranged Fatecaster pressure to clear the way, and convert objective control into points while Sorcerers stack buffs onto the Terminators. It punishes horde-heavy and chip-damage lists hard — armies relying on weight of Damage 1 shots effectively bounce off the Terminators, and the layered screening makes early trade-ins expensive. High-damage, multi-wound weapons crack it open cleanly, bypassing the detachment's save bonus entirely and threatening the expensive Terminator units that hold the whole structure together.
560: Built around Tzaangor Enlightened, Sekhetar Robots buffed by Sorcerers (including Terminators), Scarab Occult Terminators, Rubric Marines, Daemon Princes, and Magnus the Red, this list runs the Hexwarp Thrallband detachment to project a Flow of Magic across No Man's Land whenever it controls half the midfield objectives, unlocking army-wide Psychic synergies — and pairs it with Sekhetar Cohort to grant Robots Psychic attacks and WS buffs from nearby Psykers. The win condition is layered, simultaneous pressure: Robots and Terminators brawl for midfield markers to trigger and sustain Flow of Magic while Enlightened and gunline elements delete screens, forcing opponents into no-win trades. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot contest multiple objectives simultaneously against this volume of Psychic-tagged melee and ranged threat across every zone. It cracks open against fast alpha-strike lists that can collapse midfield control early and sever Flow of Magic before the kill engine comes online.
571: Built around Belisarius Cawl, multiple Skorpius Disintegrators, Ironstrider Ballistarii, Onager Dunecrawlers, and a dense supporting core of Rangers, Servitor Battleclades, and Sicarian Infiltrators, this castle plays primarily under the Lords of the Forge detachment, where Cawl and Tech-Priest Enginseer models gain 4+ Invulnerable Saves and Feel No Pain 5+, making the repair-and-hold engine genuinely hard to dismantle. The plan is to anchor a layered gunline, use Skitarii Rangers and Infiltrators to screen objectives and deny approach lanes, while the Disintegrators and Ballistarii methodically strip opposing units at range and Cawl's Baffling Data Screed harasses nearby enemy Vehicles. It punishes mid-range and slow armored lists that cannot quickly close the distance, as layered lethal fire combined with durable Tech-Priest characters makes trading piece-for-piece deeply unfavorable for the opponent. Fast alpha-strike armies or deep-striking infantry that bypass the screen and get into melee early crack it open, overwhelming the castle before repairs and firepower can stabilize.
609: Built around Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, a Blade Champion, and both the Contemptor-Achillus and Telemon Dreadnoughts, with Vertus Praetors providing fast-moving support, this list runs the Might Of The Moritoi detachment to push its WALKER units an extra 2" of movement plus bonuses to advance and charge rolls, while Shield Host's Martial Ka'tah cycling adds either critical hit generation or AP improvement to melee output. The plan is to crash elite infantry and supercharged walkers into the midboard simultaneously, using the Praetors' speed to threaten flanks while Guard and Wardens hold objectives and the Dreadnoughts crack armor and infantry in melee. It punishes slower, lower-model-count armies that cannot contest the midboard before the walkers arrive with their enhanced threat ranges, overwhelming them through multi-unit melee pressure. It cracks under alpha-strike shooting lists or anything that can isolate and remove the Dreadnoughts before they engage, since the list's scoring engine collapses without those high-value melee threats reaching combat.
584: Built around Krieg Combat Engineers, Tempestus Scions with their Command Squads, Gaunt's Ghosts, and dense banks of Krieg and Catachan Heavy Weapons Squads operating under Designation Force's Signal Flares ability on Scout Sentinels, this list floods the table with layered infantry and punishing long-range firepower. The plan is to use Signal Flares to designate priority targets, concentrate overlapping heavy weapons fire to delete threats early, and leverage Scions with Taurox transports for mobile anti-armour strikes — with Mechanised Assault's wound-roll bonus rewarding disembark-and-fire plays in roughly a third of lists. It excels against elite low-volume armies that can't efficiently clear the sheer body count, as the gunline simply reloads faster than opponents can attrition it. Aggressive close-range alpha-strike lists that collapse the screen before the heavy weapons cycle can punish it hard, since the artillery and infantry both need breathing room to output effectively.
610: Built around Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, Allarus Custodians, Blade Champions, and paired Anathema Psykana kill-squads in Witchseekers and Prosecutors, this is a transport-heavy midboard brawler that floods objectives with elite infantry delivered inside Venerable Land Raiders and on foot. The win condition is volume-of-elite-presence: stacking Null Aegis aura coverage to make Custodes units nearly unkillable in the midboard while Allarus Custodians and Blade Champions delete priority targets in melee and score through attrition and hold-more pressure. It punishes low-model elite armies that cannot generate enough attacks to chew through multiple Feel No Pain layers on 2-wound, high-save bodies across multiple squads simultaneously. It cracks open against high-volume mortal-wound-free shooting lists that simply ignore the aura benefits and grind down the small model count before Custodes can close distance.
542: Built around Chaos Rhinos shuttling Noise Marines, Chosen, and Legionaries forward alongside Chaos Bikers, Huron Blackheart, and the Masters of the Maelstrom warlord trio, anchored by Defilers and Red Corsairs Raiders punching from range. The Renegade Raiders detachment's universal Assault on Heretic Astartes ranged weapons lets this army disembark, move, and fire without penalty, while the AP-1 bonus on objective-range attacks turns massed mid-tier shooting into a grind that bleeds opponents off contested markers turn by turn. It punishes static gunlines and lightly armoured hordes that can't weather high-volume, AP-improved fire from multiple angles while cultist mobs deny space and Rhinos threaten rapid repositioning. Durable elite infantry backed by Defilers will struggle against mass high-AP anti-tank overload or fast armies that can isolate and kill the Rhinos before the payload is delivered.
471:
Built around Knight Despoilers, War Dog Karnivores, Nurglings, and Beasts of Nurgle, this is an Infernal Lance list that floods the board with Nurgle daemon chaff while swinging enormous armoured hammers into everything the opponent fields.

The plan is to use Nurglings and Beasts of Nurgle as disposable screens and objective squatters, freeing the Knights to pursue and destroy high-value targets through Malefic Surge-empowered threat projection — if the Leadership test lands, a Despoiler or Karnivore becomes a supercharged killing machine that punishes any attempt to trade efficiently.

This build absolutely brutalises elite low-volume armies by overwhelming their anti-tank budget with multiple large Knights plus a swarm of bodies that forces impossible target-priority decisions.

Against high-volume horde lists with cheap screening and volume mortal wound output, the Leadership-test gamble becomes unreliable and the daemon chaff thins faster than it can screen, leaving expensive Knights exposed.
595: Built around Indomitor Kill Teams, a Captain in Gravis Armour, Deathwatch Veterans, Watch Master, Intercessors, Incursors, Deathwatch Terminators, and Talonstrike Kill Teams under the Black Spear Task Force, this is a dense mixed-infantry gunline that floods the board with kill teams exploiting the detachment's wound-targeting mechanic — when a kill team contains models with different Toughness values, attackers must wound against the majority Toughness, making these units surprisingly durable under focused fire. The win condition is combined-arms attrition: the Tome of Ectoclades and Thief of Secrets pump output across multiple threat vectors while kill teams hold and contest objectives behind a wall of bodies. It punishes lists that rely on mid-strength weapons hitting a single toughness bracket, as the mixed-profile protection frustrates efficient wounding across the board. It cracks against elite alpha-strike armies with high-damage, high-AP weapons that bypass the wound-skew entirely and delete key units before the gunline can answer.
575: Built around Hellions, Wyches, Reavers, and Incubi ferried aboard Venoms and Raiders, this is a mass-infantry swarm pairing Exhibition of Slaughter's Lethal Hits on all Wych Cult melee attacks with Skysplinter Assault's Lance bonus on weapons after disembarking from transports. The win condition is a coordinated mid-table blitz — flood objectives with cheap bodies while Lelith, Drazhar, and Incubi use the Lance-boosted disembark window to crack elite targets and erase screens in the same activation. It punishes horde and mid-tier infantry armies brutally, stacking Lethal Hits into volume attacks to generate mortal-wound-equivalent output that overwhelms anything that isn't a Monster or Vehicle. High unit count and speed make it a terror against slower builds, but a hard alpha strike that clips the Venoms before the disembark turn hits lands shuts the engine off entirely — lose the transports, lose the Lance, and the damage ceiling collapses fast.
541: Built around Warp Talons, Raptors, a Jump Pack Chaos Lord, Cultists, Chosen, and Defilers, this is an aggressive airborne assault list that floods the midboard with flying infantry and backs them up with heavy walker support. The win condition is attrition-through-pressure: flying units crack enemy units below half-strength or into battle-shock, then the Murdertalon Raiders detachment's re-roll-hits-of-1 mechanic turns those wounded units into reliable kill targets while simultaneously making the flying units harder to shoot back. It punishes slow, high-durability gunlines that bleed wounds gradually, as Raptors and Warp Talons can exploit any half-strength trigger to snowball kills efficiently. It struggles against alpha-strike armies that can delete key flying units before they land their first charge, collapsing the half-strength engine before it gets going.
588: Built around Flawless Blades, Infractors, Lords Exultant, Tormentors, Lucius the Eternal, Defilers, and winged Daemon Princes operating under Peerless Bladesmen and Spectacle of Slaughter, this is a transport-heavy charge engine that floods the mid-table with elite melee infantry. The win condition is charging every turn: Peerless Bladesmen grants charging units either Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1, while Spectacle of Slaughter gives Flawless Blades Fights First, letting them shred anything that tries to hold the line before the opponent can swing back. It punishes elite low-model-count armies badly, as stacked charge bonuses and Fights First overwhelm small defensive units that can't absorb repeated high-quality melee pressure. Armies that can screen out charges, deny the mid-table with dense bodies, or delete transport vehicles before delivery force this list to fight on the backfoot, where its melee synergies don't trigger.
592: Built around Castellan Crowe, multiple Grand Masters and Nemesis Dreadknights in both flavours, and Purifier Squads pushing Hallowed Ground coverage across the board, this is a mobile, layered Grey Knights force that controls territory through sacred-zone expansion. The engine is Purifier positioning: spreading Hallowed Ground into No Man's Land unlocks the detachment's third condition, letting the army score while Dreadknights and Crowe apply lethal pressure from multiple angles simultaneously. It punishes horde and mid-tier infantry lists hardest, where massed Dreadknight strikes and Purifier board presence overwhelm screens before opponents can contest objectives. It cracks under concentrated elite anti-armour overload — anything that can strip Dreadknights in a single activation removes the teeth and leaves the Hallowed Ground engine underpowered.
591: Built around Paladin Squads supported by a Brother-Captain, Strike Squads, Interceptor Squads, Brotherhood Chaplain, Grand Master in Nemesis Dreadknight, Castellan Crowe, and Purifier Squads running Argent Assault and Banishers, this is a mobile psychic melee army with a hard-hitting terminator core backed by fast screening elements. The engine is Argent Assault's wound-roll boost when Paladins fight up-Toughness targets, layered with Banishers' Leadership-gated Sustained Hits on Psychic weapons to stack damage output in the fight phase against anything armoured. Interceptors and Strike Squads provide the mobility and screening depth to deny opponents easy objectives while funnelling fights toward the Paladin brick on favourable terms. It cracks open when opponents screen effectively to prevent the Paladins engaging, or when attrition across multiple turns bleeds the brick before it can trade efficiently.
594: Built around Armiger Warglaives and Armiger Helverins, this list establishes two foundation objectives at game start and dares the opponent to fight through a defensive line to contest them, while the Armigers range freely on either flank. The engine is Throne-Bonded Outriders' Ignores Cover on Bondsman-buffed Armigers: every turn, the Warglaives hunt armoured targets in the open while Helverins strip saves from units sheltering in terrain, generating relentless anti-armour pressure that funds scoring through board control rather than raw point-grabs. It punishes elite vehicle-heavy lists that need cover to survive, because Ignores Cover dismantles that defensive assumption entirely. Infantry-spam and screen-heavy armies that can flood the defensive line and deny clean Bondsman angles without exposing tanks will stretch the Armiger bubble thin and crack the scoring engine.
580: Built around Doomsday Arks, Flayed Ones, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, and the C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer, this list plants heavy artillery in a protected backfield castle while mobile threats roam forward to threaten objectives and key targets. The Doomsday Arks anchor the firebase, layering anti-tank firepower from range while Lokhust Heavy Destroyers add concentrated armour-cracking shots, and the Nightbringer threatens anything that pushes into midfield. Flayed Ones provide aggressive board pressure and objective harassment, forcing opponents to either overcommit to chasing them or cede ground to the castle. The build punishes slow, durable armies that want to grind forward into ranged fire, but aggressive alpha-strike lists that close distance quickly can outpace the damage output and crack the firebase before the heavy guns can answer.
604: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, multiple Warbosses, Boyz and Nobz crammed into Trukks and Battlewagons, Stormboyz arriving from above, and Boss Snikrot leading flanking Kommandos, this is War Horde's mass-assault engine running Sustained Hits 1 on every Ork melee weapon across a sprawling green tide. The plan is to deliver multiple independent melee threats simultaneously — transports unload into mid-board while Stormboyz and Snikrot's Kommandos hit flanks, overwhelming enemy activations and scoring through raw board control and bodies. It punishes static elite armies badly, where Sustained Hits 1 on massed attacks bleeds expensive units dry faster than they can remove the horde. Shooting-heavy armies that can strip transports before they land and board-wide blast weapons that punish tight infantry clusters are the hard counters here.
601: Built around massed Boyz squads, Gretchin screens, Ghazghkull Thraka, multiple Painboyz, Warbosses, Stormboyz, and Bigbosses flooding the midfield, this is a classic Ork green tide running War Horde — every Ork melee weapon gains Sustained Hits 1, turning raw volume of attacks into a murder machine. The plan is to crash waves of infantry into the enemy midfield behind Ghazghkull's aura support and Painboy durability buffs, grinding opponents off objectives through attrition and sheer body count. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't efficiently kill enough bodies before being swamped in melee. It struggles against high-volume shooting that deletes whole squads before contact, since losing enough bodies collapses the pressure entirely.
605: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, multiple Warbosses (including Warboss in Mega Armour), Meganobz, Nobz, Boyz, and Painboyz hauled forward in Trukks and Battlewagons, this is a mid-table brawler that floods the board with elite and horde infantry under a double Waaagh! engine — the detachment's signature ability lets a second Waaagh! fire specifically for Warboss, Nobz, and Meganobz units, stacking a second activation window on top of the first. The plan is to crash transport-delivered Meganobz and Nobz into the opponent's key units during the Waaagh! turn, clearing threats and bullying primary objectives through sheer combat dominance. It punishes elite low-model armies that struggle to withstand repeated waves of high-volume, buffed melee attacks across multiple fronts. Spread-out horde armies or fast shooting lists that strip the transports early and deny the delivery mechanism before the Waaagh! turns arrive can crack it open.
602: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Wazdakka Gutsmek, Flash Gitz, Lootas, Tankbustas, and waves of Boyz and Gretchin riding Trukks, all operating under the Freebooter Krew detachment — every unit generates Sustained Hits 1 on all attacks, and ORKS INFANTRY ranged attacks gain Assault, turning a green tide into a relentless fire-and-charge engine. The loot objective mechanic forces opponents to fight for a rotating priority marker while Ghazghkull's Waaagh! stacks a second layer of Sustained Hits 1 onto infantry shooting, creating a volume-of-fire kill chain that funds primary scoring through sheer board presence and attrition. This list punishes low-model-count elite armies brutally — the combination of mass bodies, Painboy durability buffs, and double Sustained Hits output simply overwhelms armies that can't absorb the wound flood across multiple phases. It cracks when facing aggressive alpha-strike lists that can decapitate Ghazghkull or the Painboys early, collapsing the durability layer before the Waaagh! window opens.
598:
Built around Biovores, Zoanthropes, a Neurotyrant, Raveners, The Red Terror, Neurolictors, Trygons, Hormagaunts, The Swarmlord, Lictors, and Hyperadapted Raveners, this Subterranean Assault list operates as a coordinated ambush force where Mawloc and Trygon units carry the Burrower keyword, enabling subterranean deployment pressure across the entire game, with Trygons frequently upgraded to Characters via the detachment rule — most commonly as a Trygon Prime — to carry Enhancements and lead the assault.

The plan is to flood midboard with fast melee threats arriving from multiple angles simultaneously, forcing opponents to defend everywhere while Biovores and Zoanthropes suppress from range, creating kill lanes for Raveners and The Red Terror to exploit.

This build punishes static gunlines that lack the board coverage to screen against deep-striking underground threats and infantry screens, as Neurolictors and Lictors can strip screening units to open charge lanes before the main body arrives.

It struggles against armies with robust deep strike denial, durable elite melee that can out-fight Raveners in the brawl, or heavy indirect-fire saturation that can attrition the screen units before the underground wave lands.
607: Built around Magnus the Red, Rubric Marines in Chaos Rhinos, Tzaangor Enlightened with fatecaster greatbows, Sorcerers, an Infernal Master, Scarab Occult Terminators, a winged Daemon Prince, Sekhetar Robots, and Tzaangors, all operating under Grand Coven — a detachment that cycles through powerful one-per-game command abilities to amplify the army's psychic output. The plan is to extend psychic weapon ranges and pile on lethal psychic fire from multiple angles while Magnus personally threatens to delete priority targets, with Rhino-mounted Rubrics and screen-holding Tzaangors contesting objectives to force opponents into unfavorable trades. It punishes low-volume elite armies that can't absorb sustained layered psychic shooting across multiple threat vectors simultaneously, especially when Grand Coven's range extension turns medium-range guns into long-range dominance tools. It cracks apart against fast aggressive armies that can close the distance before the psychic engine spins up, or high-mobility alpha-strike lists that isolate and delete Magnus before he generates value.
485: Built around Norn Emissaries, Norn Assimilators, Maleceptors, Tyrannofexes, Exocrines, and Biovores anchored in the Crusher Stampede detachment, this is a wall of Tyranid Monsters that gets measurably more dangerous as it takes damage — hitting and wounding more reliably below Starting Strength, while full-health units bully objectives with boosted OC. The plan is to flood mid-board with high-OC monsters early, grind through attrition trades where the detachment's wounded-monster buffs flip combat math in your favour, and delete priority targets with layered shooting from Tyrannofexes and Exocrines. It punishes armies that spread damage across multiple monsters without finishing them — half-dead Monsters hitting harder is a brutal tax on inefficient firepower. Concentrated burst damage that deletes monsters outright before the wounded buffs kick in, or elite melee lists that can simply overpower individual creatures in isolation, expose how thin the board coverage becomes when the monster count drops.
565:
Built around Defilers, Slaughterbound, Eightbound, Exalted Eightbound, Jakhals, and a Daemon Prince of Khorne under the Brazen Engines detachment, this is a wall of daemon vehicles and frenzied infantry that grinds through the midboard with layered melee threat at every point cost.

The plan is to weaponize Terror of Khorne — forcing battle-shock rolls on anything fighting the daemon vehicles — while the Eightbound and Exalted Eightbound crash into whatever the Defilers pin down, creating a cascade of melee pressure that generates Blood Tithe points to fuel sustained combat dominance.

It punishes slower, lower-model-count lists that can't weather multiple simultaneous melee engagements, particularly anything relying on morale-sensitive units that Terror of Khorne degrades further.

High-volume shooting that strips Eightbound before they engage, or extremely fast armies that contest before the melee wave arrives, pull this list apart — it has limited tools to close distance safely if screened and denied early board presence.
719: Built around Repentia Squads, Arco-Flagellants, and Celestian Sacresants alongside Morvenn Vahl and Paragon Warsuits, this list runs the Penitent Host detachment with Sacred Champions to layer melee threat across multiple unit types simultaneously. The engine is rotating Vows of Atonement each round — pushing Penitent units up the board with extended movement early, then unleashing fight-phase volume to overwhelm objectives and grind through attrition, with Hospitallers keeping key units alive long enough to swing again. Sacred Champions' +1 WS on Celestian Sacresants creates a precision melee hammer that punishes elite infantry and multi-wound infantry that can't absorb the raw number of attacks. Armies that screen effectively with cheap bodies or deny charge lanes crack this open, since the whole kill chain collapses when melee units can't reach their targets in time.
710: Built around a wall of Custodes Dreadnoughts — Contemptor-Achillus, Venerable Contemptor, Contemptor-Galatus, and Telemon variants — supported by Witchseekers, Prosecutors, and Caladius Grav-Tanks across both Silent Hunters and Solar Spearhead detachments. The plan is to flood mid-table with high-OC Vehicles boosted by Solar Spearhead's +2 Objective Control at Starting Strength, while Witchseekers use Ceaseless Vigilance to null priority threats and Achillus Dreadnoughts brawl through anything contesting. It punishes infantry-heavy gunlines that struggle to generate enough anti-tank volume to drop multiple durable Dreadnoughts before they lock down the centre. However, elite shooting lists that can efficiently crack vehicles at range will strip that OC advantage fast, and losing Dreadnoughts early collapses both the scoring engine and the threat density simultaneously.
717: Built around Morvenn Vahl, Paragon Warsuits, Celestian Sacresants, Arco-Flagellants, and a deep bench of Immolators and Castigators, this is a mobile firebase that deliberately bleeds its own units to unlock its signature buff — hitting and wounding on improved rolls once squads drop below Starting Strength. The win condition is engineering attrition on your own terms: absorb early punishment across a wide, expendable screen of infantry and transports, then release combat-hungry units at peak lethality when they're already half-dead. Immolators and Castigators provide layered skimmer fire that punishes slow, high-value targets that can't reposition out of arc, while the melee threat of Sacresants and Arco-Flagellants overloads anything relying on a thin defensive line. The list cracks when opponents can spike damage fast enough to wipe units entirely before the martyrdom bonus triggers — surgical alpha-strike armies that delete squads in one volley prevent the buff engine from ever coming online.
662: Built around Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Tempestus Scions, Hellhounds, and Tech-Priest Enginseers, this is an elite deep-strike gunline that uses the Bridgehead Strike detachment's bonus hit roll for units set up mid-game to punch far above their points value the turn they land. The win condition is hot-dropping Scions and Command Squads directly onto contested objectives, firing with enhanced accuracy before cycling the next wave in, while Hellhounds pressure screens and contest flanks to keep the scoring lanes open. It punishes horde armies and light-infantry lists ruthlessly — mass Battleline Scions with +1 OC flood objectives while hitting reliably against low-save targets. It struggles against durable vehicle-heavy lists that can absorb the alpha-strike shooting and eliminate the fragile Scions before they can be repositioned.
693: Built around Crusader Squads, Crusade Ancients, Execrators, Sword Brethren, the Emperor's Champion, Intercessors, Scouts, and Repulsor Executioners, this list runs primarily the Vindication Task Force and Wrathful Procession detachments to create a hybrid skimmer-gunline that keeps durable infantry planted on objectives while Repulsor Executioners pour heavy fire downfield. The engine is attrition-by-resilience: Ancients sitting on objectives gain wound-roll protection against high-Strength attacks, letting the footprint hold ground while Execrators and Repulsors delete threats at range, and Crusader Squads surge into contested zones to finish the scoring math. It punishes slow, low-volume shooting armies that can't crack the Ancient's on-objective damage reduction before the infantry locks them out of the primary. High-AP, high-volume melee threats that bypass the wound-roll protection entirely and collapse the transport-infantry core in one activation cycle are the clearest way to break it open.
645: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, Commander Dante, Chaplain with Jump Pack, Captain with Jump Pack, Lemartes, and Baal Predators, with Scouts and Intercessors holding the deck — this is a multi-wave jump pack assault force spread across several detachment flavors, most commonly Legacy of Grace granting +1 to advance and charge rolls for Infantry Characters. The plan is to flood mid-board with fast melee threats, using Dante and the Chaplain to buff Death Company and Sanguinary Guard into lethal charge threats that delete priority targets and collapse opponent scoring lanes in the fight phase. It punishes slow, static gunlines that cannot reposition away from repeated charge waves, particularly lists relying on massed light infantry or mid-tier vehicles that the Baal Predators and mobile anti-armor elements can strip efficiently. However, it struggles against deep-strike denial screens and hard-hitting alpha-strike armies that can cripple the jump pack core before it engages, as losing key Character buffers mid-list gutters the entire kill chain.
667: Built around Bloodcrushers, Lords of Change, Bloodthirster, Be'lakor, and Screamers, this Cavalcade of Chaos list runs a multi-wave daemonic cavalry and monster engine where every unit threatens both shooting and combat after falling back — the defining ability of the detachment turning disengagements into second strikes rather than retreats. The win condition is layered threat overload: Bloodcrushers and Screamers crash into midboard objectives while Lords of Change and Be'lakor project psychic and shooting pressure, forcing opponents to answer too many vectors simultaneously. It punishes slow, static lines that can't generate enough bodies to hold multiple objectives, bleeding them dry through relentless re-engagement. It cracks open against elite alpha-strike lists that can delete key mounted units before the fall-back-and-shoot engine comes online, leaving the cavalry threat neutered before it establishes board presence.
666: Built around Rotigus, multiple Great Unclean Ones, Plaguebearers, Beasts of Nurgle, Nurglings, and Sloppity Bilepipers, this is a mass-Nurgle horde that floods the table with disgustingly durable bodies across every tier of the force org. The win condition is attrition through layered lethality — bloated Monsters anchor midfield while Plaguebearers and Nurglings sit on objectives and Beasts of Nurgle threaten charges, grinding opponents down through sheer volume of wounds that must be answered. It punishes lists that rely on concentrated elite firepower, because there are simply too many high-toughness, high-wound targets to prioritise efficiently before objectives slip away. Armies with reliable mortal wound output, high volumes of multi-damage shooting, or strong board-wide debuffs can overwhelm the build by bypassing its layered durability and collapsing its scoring footprint before reinforcements arrive.
668: Built around Screamers, Lords of Change, Flamers, Kairos Fateweaver, Pink Horrors, and Beasts of Nurgle, this Tzeentch-heavy daemon list runs Scintillating Legion as its engine, banking Flux tokens to re-roll critical dice at any point in the sequence — hits, wounds, saves, damage — giving it consistent output across a broad toolkit of threats. The plan is to advance Battleline units under Warptide to keep Assault shooting mobile, flood mid-table with horrors and Screamers for objective control, and let double Lords of Change and Flamers deliver layered lethal damage from multiple angles simultaneously. It punishes lists that rely on one or two key defensive rolls, since Flux token re-rolls can crack armour saves or force wound rolls through on demand. Armies that can alpha-strike the Flamers and Lords of Change before Flux tokens are spent, or that bring enough volume to overwhelm the horde screens faster than Beasts of Nurgle can absorb punishment, will find the re-roll economy runs dry at the worst moment.
664: Built around Bloodcrushers, Beasts of Nurgle, Flesh Hounds, a Rendmaster on Blood Throne, Skullmaster, Bloodthirster, Be'lakor, Plaguebearers, Nurglings, and a Great Unclean One, this is a mounted-heavy Cavalcade of Chaos list stuffed with Nurgle durability and Khorne aggression in equal measure. The engine is relentless threat saturation — fast MOUNTED units fall back and charge freely, keeping pressure on multiple objectives simultaneously while layered lethality from both Khorne shock cavalry and Nurgle attrition forces opponents into impossible priority decisions. It punishes lists that rely on fragile shooting phases or isolated defensive screens, since the sheer volume of durable, mobile bodies overwhelms piecemeal removal and recontests objectives before the opponent can stabilize. It cracks under concentrated high-volume anti-infantry overload that can strip Plaguebearers and Nurglings off objectives while simultaneously outranging the charge-reliant cavalry core.
665:
Built around Plaguebearers, Nurglings, Beasts of Nurgle, Bloodletters, a Bloodthirster, and Be'lakor, this is a mass-horde army running Shadow Legion with the Warptide sub-detachment fuelling aggressive advance-and-charge plays across multiple battleline units simultaneously.

The plan is to flood the midfield with overlapping bodies — Plaguebearers and Nurglings grinding objectives while Bloodletters and the Bloodthirster threaten lethal melee escalation, with Be'lakor providing a mobile command-and-threaten presence that Fade to Darkness and Leaping Shadows keep slippery and hard to pin down.

It punishes low-model-count lists that cannot contest every objective simultaneously, leveraging layered lethality and sheer unit density to trade efficiently and bleed opponents dry on secondaries.

It cracks under concentrated high-volume anti-infantry firepower that can strip hordes before they engage, or against fast alpha-strike lists that delete Be'lakor and the Bloodthirster early and collapse the offensive threat before the grind kicks in.
653: Built around Vashtorr the Arkifane, Defilers, Venomcrawlers, Warpsmiths, and Cultist Mobs under the Soulforged Warpack detachment, this list floods the board with Heretic Astartes Daemon Vehicles that leverage Dark Pact contracts to spike Wound rolls and Attacks simultaneously — turning each activation into a burst of amplified output. Vashtorr and Warpsmiths keep the metal horde operational while Cultist Mobs screen objectives and eat chaff duty, freeing the vehicles to hunt priority targets. The build punishes mechanised and heavy-armour lists hard, stacking mobile anti-armour pressure across multiple chassis that are difficult to prioritise and expensive to remove efficiently. It cracks when faced with reliable long-range shooting that can strip vehicles before contracts come online, or volume anti-tank that outpaces the Warpsmith's ability to sustain the battlegroup.
647: Built around Abaddon the Despoiler, Huron Blackheart, Chosen, Defilers, Cultist Mobs, Red Corsairs Raiders, and Masters of the Maelstrom under Pactbound Zealots, this list floods the table with bodies while parking heavy walkers in fire lanes. The engine is Pactbound Zealots' Lethal Hits on melee attacks triggering on 5+, letting Abaddon and Chosen shred armour and elite infantry in combat while Defilers hammer from range and Cultists drown objectives in cheap wounds. It punishes gunlines and horde armies alike — too many targets to prioritise, too many walkers to ignore, and Lethal Hits making even glancing contact dangerous against multi-wound units. Concentrated high-AP shooting or fast melee threats that can isolate Abaddon before he engages will crack it open, as the combat punch collapses without its anchor character.
470: Built around a full pack of War Dog Karnivores, Brigands, Executioners, and Stalkers screened by Cultist Mobs, this is a relentless mechanised swarm that leverages the Houndpack Lance's ability to designate a target unit each Command phase, granting every War Dog attacking it Sustained Hits 1 and focusing the entire pack's firepower into a single kill chain. The win condition is sequential deletion — pick the most threatening enemy unit, pile Sustained Hits onto it, erase it, then repeat, while Cultists hold objectives and absorb return fire. It punishes armour-heavy lists brutally, stacking mobile anti-tank dakka across five distinct War Dog chassis that can threaten from multiple angles simultaneously. Where it cracks is against elite infantry hordes or dense screening that splits the pack's attention and forces the designation ability onto lower-value targets, bleeding efficiency until the delete chain collapses.
649: Built around Huron Blackheart, Abaddon the Despoiler, double Chosen squads, Possessed, and a Defiler backed by cheap Cultist and Red Corsairs Raider screens, this list plays either Creations of Bile or Huron's Marauders detachments to juice its Heretic Astartes Infantry core. The plan is to flood mid-table with expendable bodies via Masters of the Maelstrom and cultist screens while Abaddon and Chosen punch through the opposing line to generate primary and secondary scoring from dominant board position. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies that cannot answer multiple independent melee threats simultaneously — Possessed and Chosen force overextended target priority while Abaddon cleans up. The weakness is volume firepower from gunline armies that can strip screens early, leaving the melee hammers exposed and stranded without the board saturation that makes the engine function.
635: Built around Land Speeder Vengances, Land Speeders, and Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes alongside Azrael, Deathwing Knights, and Inner Circle Companions, this is a Darkflight Pursuit list that floods the board with Ravenwing skimmers whose ranged attacks ignore cover on everything they target. The plan is to use the mobile Ravenwing firepower to strip infantry and light vehicles off objectives while the Deathwing Knights and companions — buffed by Azrael's aura — hold or contest whatever the speeders clear, converting board control into scoring. The Ignores Cover blanket punishes armies that rely on dense terrain or fortified infantry screens to survive shooting, while the Deathwing Knights provide a durable melee hammer that most MSU lists cannot trade into efficiently. However, the list thins out fast against elite anti-tank overload lists, since the speeders are individually fragile and losing even two or three early collapses both the firepower base and the objective pressure simultaneously.
652: Built around a pair of Defilers and Venomcrawlers alongside Abaddon the Despoiler, Kravek Morne, Cultist Mobs, and Nurglings and Beasts of Nurgle holding the flanks, this Pactbound Zealots list floods the table with durable, high-value threats at every range band. The plan is to overwhelm opponent priority targeting — Defilers and Venomcrawlers threaten armour from range while Abaddon and the melee core crash forward, exploiting Pactbound Zealots' Lethal Hits on a 5+ in melee to crack anything they reach. It punishes gunlines and vehicle-heavy lists that can't kill two Defilers, two Venomcrawlers, and a tanky melee beatstick simultaneously, forcing brutal trade decisions every turn. Lists with strong mortal wound output or elite melee that can isolate and delete the daemon engines before the brawl materialises will dismantle the kill chain before it gets rolling.
638: Built around Ravenwing Black Knights, Ravenwing Command Squads, Outrider Squads, and a leadership trio of Sammael, Lion El'Jonson, and Azrael, this is a fast, character-stacked biker force that floods the midfield with high-mobility Adeptus Astartes cavalry. The win condition is sustained pressure through repeated close-range combat and skimmer fire — Command Squads and Black Knights deliver buffed melee and shooting while heroic characters amplify key units each turn to grind down whatever contest your bikes are sitting on. It punishes slow, infantry-heavy gunlines that can't reposition fast enough to deny the midfield, as the sheer volume of mobile bodies and layered character auras overwhelm static defensive setups. Against armies that can alpha-strike the bike screen or crack the character stack early — particularly high-volume mortal wound output or deep-striking assault threats — the list loses its coherence quickly since the buffs and board presence depend on keeping expensive characters alive.
640: Built around Librarians in Terminator armour, Inner Circle Companions, Deathwing Knights, and Azrael, this is a psychic-powered elite infantry list running the Inner Circle Task Force with Librarius Conclave as its engine. The core plan is to flex the Vowed objective mechanic each turn — locking down a held objective defensively or swinging onto uncontrolled ones aggressively — while the Librarius Conclave buffs the entire psyker stack with Divination or Biomancy to either sharpen the kill chain or surge Terminators into scoring position. It punishes slow, durable gunlines that expect to trade efficiently, because stacked re-rolls and movement buffs let the elite melee and transport infantry force trades on Dark Angels' terms. Spread or horde lists that contest multiple objectives simultaneously expose the build's limited body count, overwhelming its Vowed objective switching before it can stabilize.
451: Built around Lady Malys, Drazhar, Archons riding in Venoms, Incubi, Wyches, Ravagers, Mandrakes, Scourges, Reavers, and Hellions, this is a high-density Drukhari swarm that layers skimmer-delivered firepower over a mass of cheap bodies. The core engine is Exhibition Of Slaughter's Lethal Hits on Wych Cult melee combined with Skysplinter Assault's Lance on disembarking units, turning every Venom drop into a precision kill spike that punishes anything short of a Monster or Vehicle in melee. It thrives against elite infantry armies that can't absorb simultaneous threats from multiple flanks — the sheer number of units forces prioritisation errors while Ravagers and Scourges strip armour from range. It cracks against durable vehicle-heavy lists where Lethal Hits don't trigger and concentrated firepower can delete the fragile skimmers before the disembark payoff resolves.
596: Built around Librarians (both on foot and in Terminator armour), Deathwatch Veterans, Indomitor Kill Teams, Deathwatch Terminator Squads, and Sternguard Veterans operating under the Bastion Task Force and Librarius Conclave detachments, this is a heavy gunline that floods the board with elite infantry crammed into transports. The engine is Bastion Task Force's Battleline rule — Intercessors and other Battleline units shoot and perform Actions after Advancing or Falling Back, keeping the scoring machine running while the Librarius Conclave cycles psychic disciplines (Divination's re-rolls for volume shooting, Biomancy for repositioning) to maximize firepower from stationary kill teams and Veterans. It punishes static elite armies that can't threaten the transport bubble, overwhelming them with layered small-arms and special weapons before they close distance.
