Armies that can strip transports early or apply volume mortal-wound pressure crack it open, since the infantry inside loses both its mobility and its action-economy engine simultaneously.
654: Built around Lady Malys, Drazhar, Incubi, Wyches, and a swarm of Venoms and Raiders, this is a transport-infantry blitz running Skysplinter Assault and Exhibition of Slaughter in tandem — every unit that disembarks swings melee weapons with Lance while Wych Cult fighters stack Lethal Hits against everything that isn't a Monster or Vehicle. The plan is to flood the midboard with fast skimmers, then cascade disembarks that hit with Ignores Cover shooting and Lance melee simultaneously, burying opponents in volume before they can stabilize. It punishes mid-density infantry armies that lack the raw defense to absorb multiple stacked lethality vectors across several activation windows. Armies that can alpha-strike the transport layer before disembarkation, or that field enough Monster and Vehicle keywords to blunt the Lethal Hits engine, will crack the plan open before the cascade ever fires.
672: Built around multiple squads of Infractors riding Chaos Rhinos, Lords Exultant as beat-stick attachments, Tormentors, Defilers, winged Daemon Princes of Slaanesh, and Noise Marines, this is a Coterie of the Conceited transport-infantry hammer that floods the midboard with elite melee and mobile anti-armour threats. The engine is the Pact point economy: by pledging realistic kill numbers each round and consistently delivering them through coordinated charge waves and Defiler fire support, the build accumulates Pact points to fuel escalating power, while Rhinos deliver Infractors into contact before the opponent can screen effectively. It punishes slower gunlines and low-model-count elite armies that can't prevent the initial wave from making contact and racking up the kills needed to hit the pledge threshold. The build cracks when fast, high-volume chaff screens deny early charges and break the pledge — if the kill count falls short, the Pact engine stalls and the list loses its snowball.
675: Built around Chaos Spawn, Infractors, Lords Exultant, Tormentors, Defilers, Flawless Blades, Noise Marines, and Lucius the Eternal, all ferried forward in Rhinos with a winged Daemon Prince providing mobile threat, this is a mid-table brawler that floods objectives with cheap, durable chaff while elite melee infantry do the killing. The core engine is Infractors and Tormentors piling out of transports to contest and fight, with Spawn soaking return fire and Lords Exultant amplifying nearby units into dangerous combat threats. It punishes infantry-heavy armies that can't clear durable chaff efficiently, letting Spawn screen key pieces while Flawless Blades and Noise Marines grind through lighter targets. Armies that pack high-volume anti-armour or elite melee that ignores its screening layer can crack the transport bubble early and strand key units before they reach engagement range.
633: Built around Achilles Ridgerunners, Neophyte Hybrids, Purestrain Genestealers, Patriarch, Benefictus, Hyperadapted Raveners, Acolyte Hybrids, Deathleaper, Atalan Jackals, and the Red Terror, this list exploits the Final Day detachment to flood the table with both Genestealer Cult units and borrowed Tyranid Vanguard Invader muscle simultaneously. The win condition is attrition through volume — Neophytes hold and self-sustain via Xenocult Masses healing in terrain while Raveners, Purestrains, and Acolytes with hand flamers hammer mid-board brawls and the Ridgerunners deliver mobile anti-armour pressure. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't clear waves fast enough, generating lethal close-range threat from multiple angles while objectives stay capped. However, massed mortal wounds, blast weapons, and anything that denies terrain placement cracks the Neophyte sustain engine and deflates the horde's staying power quickly.
688: Built around Nemesis Dreadknights, Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, and Interceptor Squads screened by Strike Squads, this is a mobile hammer list that floods the board with heavy walkers and teleporting infantry across a detachment-agnostic framework of Immaterial Interdiction and Sanctic Spearhead. The plan is to leverage Sanctic Spearhead's 6" Advance bonus and Assault conversion on Grey Knights Vehicles to drive Dreadknights into mid-board early, then use Interceptor surge moves to threaten objectives and force unfavorable trades while the Grand Masters amplify the kill chain. It punishes slower armoured lists that cannot contest mid-board efficiently, as multiple high-damage walkers advancing at threat ranges most opponents aren't built to handle across the whole table. However, mass high-volume shooting or deep-strike denial armies that can isolate and focus individual Dreadknights before they consolidate will crack the list open, since losing even one walker early collapses the damage math significantly.
634: Built around Achilles Ridgerunners, Purestrain Genestealers, Acolyte Hybrids, Neophyte Hybrids, Atalan Jackals, and Goliath Rockgrinders, this is a mass-body cult list blending a heavy gunline with a swarming melee threat, running Outlander Claw most often with Xenocult Masses or Purestrain Broodswarm as a second layer. The plan is to flood objectives with bodies that actively resist displacement — Atalan Jackals lock down controlled markers through the Outlander Claw ability while Neophyte blobs regenerate wounds inside terrain, and Genestealers cycle back into Strategic Reserves after combat to threaten re-engagement every turn. It punishes armies that rely on clearing objectives sequentially, because replacing casualties faster than an opponent can produce them means the cult's Objective Control advantage compounds across scoring phases. Armies with high-volume mortal wounds or fight-first abilities crack it open by bypassing the wound-regeneration loop and pulling Genestealers into combats they cannot escape cleanly.
689: Built around Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Purgation Squads, Castellan Crowe with Purifier Squads, Strike Squads, and Brotherhood Terminators operating under Brotherhood Strike and Fires of Purgation. The plan is to deep strike aggressively — leveraging Brotherhood Strike's re-rolls on both hit and wound for arriving units — while Purgation Squads pin key targets and force battle-shock rolls at -1, stripping enemy board control and creating kill windows for the Dreadknights to exploit. This build punishes mid-board infantry-heavy armies that rely on coherent battleshock immunity, as the pin-and-shock engine degrades their activation quality while mobile Dreadknights clean up. It cracks open against concentrated high-AP elite shooting, which can pick apart the relatively small model count before the deep strike payload lands.
615: Built around Berehk Stornbröw, Einhyr Hearthguard, Cthonian Beserks, Kâhls, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and Hekaton Land Fortresses under the Hearthguard Covenant, this list blends a punishing midfield brawl core with a heavy fire-support backbone. The engine is close-range attrition: Hearthguard Covenant's wound-roll-1 rerolls within 9" reward aggressive pushes, while Berehks contest and trade efficiently as Thunderkyn and Land Fortresses strip armour from range. It punishes slow, durable elite lists that can't prevent the midfield collision — once Beserks and Hearthguard are in the 9" bubble, the reroll pressure becomes overwhelming. However, fast alpha-strike armies that eliminate the brawl units before they close, or screens that keep the bubble threat at arm's length, expose the list's dependence on proximity to deliver its full wound output.
700: Built around the Cerastus Knight Lancer as its engine, this list pairs one or two of these fast, hard-hitting nobles with a flexible supporting cast of Questoris knights and Armigers drawn from across the roster. The Questoris Companions detachment drives the win condition by stacking Oaths — fulfilling one immediately generates another, creating a compounding chain of bonuses that keeps each knight operating at peak efficiency turn after turn while they pressure objectives and hunt priority targets. The Pennant of Silvered Fury, taken in nearly two-thirds of lists, amplifies this momentum, and the overall toolkit punishes armies that rely on a few expensive, hard-to-replace units by overwhelming them with layered anti-armour threats from multiple angles simultaneously. Where it struggles is against lists that can consistently deny Oath fulfillment or swarm it with cheap, numerous bodies that drain activations and contest objectives faster than giant knights can clear them.
621: Built around Hekaton Land Fortresses, Hernkyn Pioneers, Kapricus Carriers, Arkanyst Evaluators, Einhyr Hearthguard, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and a sprawling mass of supporting infantry, this is a dense mid-table brawler that floods the board with bodies and armoured platforms simultaneously. The win condition is volume: park Hekatons and Sagitaurs in scoring positions, screen with Pioneer and Yaegir chaff, and let the Thunderkyn and Hearthguard grind out firepower at close-to-mid range while the sheer number of units contests every objective. It punishes armies that struggle to clear mass bodies efficiently, using redundant threats across multiple chassis to overload removal priority. It cracks against elite alpha-strike lists and high-AP firepower that can simultaneously kill vehicles and delete infantry screens before the midgame grind gets established.
617: Built around Hernkyn Pioneers, Kapricus Carriers, Hernkyn Yaegirs, Cthonian Beserks, Hekaton Land Fortresses, Einhyr Hearthguard, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and a dense supporting cast, this Farseekers list plays a fast, aggressive midboard brawl where every HERNKYN unit gets +1 to hit within 12" — rewarding close-range pressure over static gunline play. The win condition is flooding the midboard early with Pioneers and Carriers, generating YP through kills via the Needgaârd or Mercenary Oathband secondary detachment, then leveraging that YP economy to fuel sustained board control and objective conversion. It punishes infantry-heavy and low-armour lists badly, stacking layered lethality from close-range skimmer fire, Thunderkyn heavy weapons, and Berserks crashing into anything that tries to hold the centre. Durable elite armies that can weather the initial push and lock down the midboard deny the engine its kill triggers and leave the list overextended.
620: Built around Hernkyn Pioneers, Hernkyn Yaegirs, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Hekaton Land Fortresses, Kapricus Carriers, and a deep supporting cast of Hearthkyn Warriors, Einhyr Hearthguard, and Arkanyst Evaluators, the Farseekers detachment delivers its central rule: Hernkyn units hit on 2s at close range, making the Pioneer screen a punishing offensive threat rather than passive chaff. The win condition is controlling mid-board space with layered, interlocking fire — Pioneers and Yaegirs flush enemies out of cover while Thunderkyn and Land Fortresses hammer exposed units, generating YP through kills that fuel secondary Oathband abilities. This punishes static gunlines and low-model-count elite armies brutally, as the sheer volume of accurate short-range fire overwhelms elite saves. Armies that deny the 12" engagement window through long-range alpha strikes or deep deployment strip the +1 hit bonus entirely, leaving the Pioneer core underperforming before it can close.
619: Built around Ûthar the Destined, Einhyr Hearthguard, Kâhl characters, and a heavy transport backbone of Hekaton Land Fortresses and Sagitaurs, this list plays a punishing mid-board brawl under the Hearthguard Covenant's close-range wound reroll, pushing elite infantry into the 9" threat bubble where every shot hits harder. The win condition is sustained close-range attrition — trading efficiently through repeated Judgment tokens while threatening to flip contested objectives with durable, hard-hitting elites offloading from transports. It punishes lists that can't project durable bodies across the mid-table, overwhelming lighter infantry screens and medium-armour warbands through sheer volume of re-rolled wound rolls at close quarters. Spread-out, high-model-count armies that deny the 9" engagement range and force the Hearthguard to shoot long crack this open, starving the core wound-reroll engine and outpacing its scoring on isolated objectives.
616: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Hekaton Land Fortresses, and waves of Cthonian Beserks, Hearthkyn Warriors, and Hernkyn screening units operating under the Hearthband detachment, this list floods the midboard with durable, aggressive bodies backed by heavy firepower. The win condition is strangling the opponent's scoring by contesting objectives with cheap screens — Pioneers, Yaegirs, Hearthkyn — while the Hearthguard and Fortresses grind through whatever holds them, using Hearthband's AP improvement on Hearthguard attacks to crack armour that would otherwise shrug them off. It punishes elite, low-model-count lists that can't match the sheer objective-holding footprint and struggle against anti-tank overload from the Thunderkyn and Fortresses simultaneously. Lists that drop fast, hard alpha strikes or flood the board with equivalent numbers crack it open by denying the midboard setup before the screening layers can establish control.
618: Built around Cthonian Beserks, Sagitaurs, Hearthkyn Warriors, Hernkyn Yaegirs, Hernkyn Pioneers, Hekaton Land Fortresses, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and support characters, this is a mechanised mid-table brawler that uses Scouts 6" on every Sagitaur to crash transports packed with Beserks and infantry into the opponent's face on turn one. The plan is to overwhelm mid-board objectives through sheer transported threat density — Beserks disembark into melee while Thunderkyn and Land Fortresses provide mobile anti-armour fire to strip away screening vehicles and expose soft targets. It punishes slow or static gunlines that cannot reposition to avoid the early-turn surge of embarked threats arriving ahead of schedule. Armies with strong alpha-strike deep strike or high-volume anti-infantry that can shred transports before they unload will crack this list open by stranding its passengers in the open.
455: Built around Skorpekh Lords, Skorpekh Destroyers, Nekrosor Ammentar, the Nightbringer, Void Dragon, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Hexmark Destroyer, Technomancer, and Imotekh, all running Cursed Legion with most lists adding Skyshroud Spearhead for Tomb Blades deep-strike pressure — this is a mobile, multi-threat melee and shooting beatdown list. The win condition is chaining Cursed Legion's escalating Strength bonus: destroy or halve a unit and every subsequent Destroyer Cult attack that turn gains +2 Strength on top of the base +2, creating a snowballing kill chain that rewards early aggression into clustered threats. It punishes mid-density armies that present multiple killable units in sequence, since each successful engagement supercharges the next strike. It cracks against elite low-model-count lists that deny the chain's trigger and against boards where opponents can isolate and trade into the Destroyers piecemeal before the snowball gets rolling.
659:
Built around the Void Dragon, Nightbringer, Deceiver, one or more Transcendent C'tan, Flayed Ones, and Ophydian Destroyers, this list fields an overwhelming mass of individually powerful god-monsters and deep-striking melee threats with no single anchor that defines its identity across all lists.

The win condition is elite-unit removal and objective denial by simultaneous pressure — multiple C'tan hit different table quadrants while Flayed Ones and Ophydian Destroyers deep strike directly onto contested objectives, forcing opponents to split answers they rarely have in sufficient volume.

It punishes lists that rely on a single elite damage dealer or centralized screen, since the sheer number of independent C'tan threats guarantees at least two or three engagements the opponent simply cannot adequately answer in the same turn.

Its critical vulnerability is high-volume, point-efficient anti-tank firepower spread across the army: losing one C'tan is survivable, but concentrated shooting that degrades two or three simultaneously collapses the pressure engine before the melee threats can close distance.
658: Built around the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, the Nightbringer, the Deceiver, and Imotekh the Stormlord — with half of lists also running a Transcendent C'tan — this is a Pantheon of Woe monster-mash that floods the board with Necrons Monsters. The win condition is the Distortion Fields aura: park multiple C'tan within 6" of priority targets to stack AP improvement across every attack, then let the shards' varied damage profiles dismantle whatever the opponent tried to protect. Opposing armies built around high-toughness, low-save elite infantry or vehicles are punished hardest, since Distortion Fields effectively strips away their defensive profile for free. Swarm armies that spread wide deny the aura clustering this list needs, and anything that can alpha-strike a C'tan before the aura activates removes the build's AP engine before it fires.
603: Built around Gretchin screens, Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Lootas, Flash Gitz, Tankbustas, Boyz mobs, and Ghazghkull Thraka leading the whole circus, this is a mass-horde gunline that floods the table with bodies while stacking serious ranged output from multiple directions. The win condition is layered threat saturation — Gretchin and Boyz clog midfield objectives while Lootas, Flash Gitz, and Shokk Attack Guns punish anything that tries to push through, with Ghazghkull enabling the Waaagh! to push ranged units into Sustained Hits territory on top of whatever detachment bonus applies. It punishes slow, durable elite armies that can't clear volume efficiently — drowning high-toughness targets in sheer volume of fire and melee mob pressure simultaneously. Mobility and alpha-strike armies that can bypass the screen and isolate the shooters, or precise mortal-wound output that deletes key characters, will crack the backline before the gunline stabilises.
702: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, Flash Gitz, Warboss, Bannernob, Nobz, Breaka Boyz, and waves of Boyz and Gretchin riding Trukks and Battlewagons under the Freebooter Krew detachment, this is a mid-board brawler that floods the table with Sustained Hits 1 attacks across every Infantry, Mounted, and Walker unit whenever they sit on the loot objective. The win condition is controlling the designated loot objective to trigger that army-wide Sustained Hits 1 bonus, then funneling Ghazghkull's retinue and transported mobs into melee to delete priority targets while Kommandos threaten secondaries from unexpected angles. It punishes static gunlines that can't clear massed bodies fast enough, overwhelming objective holders with sheer volume of Sustained attacks from both ranged Flash Gitz and close-combat mobs simultaneously. However, elite armies that can surgically remove the loot objective holder or tie up transports before the mob disembarks crack this list open by denying the Sustained Hits engine and stranding key combat units out of position.
677: Built around multiple Librarians buffing Intercessors, Scout Squads, and Bladeguard Veterans, this list floods mid-table with durable infantry bodies screened by cheap scouts while psyker-fuelled disciplines rotate between movement, accuracy, and firepower depending on the matchup. The win condition is objective saturation through volume — layered infantry screens hold secondaries while Bladeguard punch forward to lock enemy scoring units in melee and Librarian buffs convert mid-strength firepower into meaningful damage trades. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear numerous tough infantry blobs, particularly when Divination Discipline turns mass bolt fire into a reliable grind. However, it cracks under high-volume mortal wound output or blast weapons that make the infantry density a liability rather than a strength.
678: Built around Marneus Calgar, Captain Titus, Scout Squads, Wardens of Ultramar, and Bladeguard Veterans, this Reclamation Force list plays a grinding melee-and-objective stranglehold game with a durable midfield core. The detachment's twin engines — AP improvement on melee attacks near objectives and a defensive buff when holding controlled markers — reward fighting from your scoring positions, making every contested objective a trade in your favour. It punishes heavy gunlines, skimmer-heavy armies, and mass-horde lists by forcing those opponents to come into melee range of buffed, resilient infantry that hit harder while standing on objectives. However, it is relatively slow and lacks elite-level shooting, meaning alpha-strike armies or fast, mobile forces can strip your objective control before the melee buffs come online.
686: Built around Land Speeders, Scout Squads, Intercessor Squads, and Storm Speeder Hammerstrikes operating under the Fulguris Task Force detachment, which grants every Speeder unit an ingress move in the first Movement phase — effectively deploying your entire mobile gun platform ahead of schedule. The plan is to open turn one with a flood of anti-armour firepower from deep inside the opponent's half while cheap Scout and Intercessor screens lock down objectives and deny counter-pressure. This build punishes gunline and vehicle-heavy lists badly, as the ingress move circumvents traditional deployment spacing and lets Hammerstrikes threaten high-value targets before the opponent can reposition. It struggles against aggressive melee armies that can absorb the alpha strike and crash into its relatively fragile Speeder units before Scouts and Intercessors can create enough space to keep them alive.
681: Built around a core of Librarians (including one in Terminator armour), Sternguard Veterans, Bladeguard Veterans, Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, and cheap Scout and Intercessor screens, the Librarius Conclave cycles through Psychic Disciplines each round — Divination for re-rolls when shooting, Biomancy for extra movement when repositioning, Pyromancy when it needs to clear screens — while Fusillade on the dominant Librarian amplifies gunline output turn after turn. The win condition is flexible shooting volume backed by durable objective presence: Bladeguard hold points under fire while Sternguard and the discipline-buffed psykers pour accurate, high-volume shots into whatever the opponent values most. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies that can't absorb sustained re-rolling fire across multiple phases and struggle to dislodge entrenched objective holders. It cracks against fast, high-damage alpha-strike lists that can kill the Librarians before their discipline rotations compound — remove the psykers and the whole engine flatlines.
679:
Built around Intercessor Squads, Scout Squads, and Repulsor Executioners, this is a terrain-hugging gunline that turns every piece of cover into a fortified firebase — the Ceramite Sentinels detachment grants Adeptus Astartes units re-rolls of 1 to hit and wound while inside terrain, and the Entrenched keyword when they hold that ground without moving in.

The win condition is simple and brutal: park Repulsor Executioners and infantry in terrain, pour sustained re-rolled fire downrange, and dare the opponent to come dig them out under fire.

It punishes aggressive melee and alpha-strike armies that have to cross open ground, layering skimmer fire and heavy gunline output against anything forced to close the distance.

Its weakness is mobility — a deep-strike denial or fast objective-grab list that can contest multiple terrain features simultaneously will strand Entrenched units out of position, stripping the re-roll engine right when it matters most.
695: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators in multiple squads, Logan Grimnar, Ragnar Blackmane, Arjac Rockfist, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Battle Leaders, Intercessors, and Blood Claws, this is a Saga of the Great Wolf elite infantry list that floods mid-table with tough, character-buffed combat units. The win condition is controlling the mid-board through layered melee threats — Terminators and Headtakers crashing into priority targets while the rotating Hunting Pack selections like Encircling Jaws keep the charge train alive turn after turn. It punishes slower, lower-model-count lists that can't absorb simultaneous pressure from multiple elite hammer units hitting from different angles. However, it struggles against high-volume shooting or elite gunlines that can pick apart its expensive infantry before they close, since the build has little ability to hide its pieces or threaten at range.
680: Built around Caanok Var, Terminator Assault Squads, and a dense core of Librarians, Scouts, Intercessors, and Sternguard Veterans operating under the Hammer of Avernii detachment, this list plays as a layered gunline that can punch forward in close combat when the moment demands. The engine is Caanok Var's RECALCULATING ability chaining Oath of Moment targets in sequence, keeping the re-roll-wounds-of-1 bonus live across multiple kills per game while Sternguard and Terminator Assault Squads exploit each freshly painted target. It punishes mid-range infantry-heavy lists badly, leveraging transport-loaded bodies and sustained wound re-rolls to grind through screens and primary holders alike. However, elite low-model-count armies that can neutralise Caanok Var early collapse the chain entirely, stranding Terminators without their wound-fishing support.
676: Built around Infernus Squads, Bladeguard Veterans, Librarians, and a Land Raider Redeemer, this list weaponizes the Firestorm Assault Force's core rule to fire heavy weapons after advancing and spike Strength on anything within 12", turning short-range shooting into a brutal close-quarters execution engine. The plan is to push the Redeemer forward as a transport and fire platform, unload Bladeguard or Infernus Squads into the teeth of the enemy, and delete key targets through volume of high-Strength assault fire at point-blank range. It punishes slow, dense armies — hordes and heavily-armoured infantry clumps — that cannot escape the 12" Strength bonus window before taking catastrophic casualties. Lists that can screen the approach, force engagement at range, or apply early pressure before the Redeemer delivers its cargo will crack this open, since the entire kill chain collapses if the short-range band is never safely reached.
682: Built around Darnath Lysander, Terminator Assault Squads, Terminator Squads, Vanguard Veterans with jump packs, Bladeguard Veterans, and a Librarian, this is a dense, multi-wave melee and fire-support list running the Emperor's Shield detachment, which hands Lysander full wound re-rolls against the Oath of Moment target and gives the broader army wound-1 re-rolls on the same target. The plan is to identify a priority threat early, stack Oath of Moment wound re-rolls onto it through Lysander's enhanced version, and bulldoze it off objectives while Terminator bricks hold ground and jump infantry contest flanks. It punishes armies that rely on a single powerful anchor — monsters, vehicles, elite infantry blocks — because concentrating the re-roll engine on one target makes that unit collapse disproportionately fast. It struggles against fast, spread-out armies that deny clean Oath of Moment focus and can kite the slow Terminator core, bleeding it for points across multiple objectives before it can consolidate.
528: Built around Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Arjac Rockfist, and Grey Hunters operating under the Saga Of The Great Wolf detachment's rotating Hunting Pack buffs, with Veterans Of The Fang appearing in nearly three-quarters of lists to let Grey Hunters perform actions without sacrificing their shooting. The plan is to flood mid-table with transported infantry and elite melee threats, cycling Hunting Packs each Command phase to grant re-rolls on Advances and Charges when closing distance, then shifting to accuracy buffs once locked in combat. It punishes slower, denser infantry hordes that can't survive the combined weight of multiple Terminator and Headtaker units crashing in simultaneously with re-roll support. Armies that can screen effectively against the charge or apply serious anti-tank pressure to the transport layer before the infantry deploys will disrupt the timing engine this list depends on.
614: Built around Commander Farsight, Coldstar Commanders, Crisis Starscythe, Sunforge, and Fireknife Battlesuits, Stealth Battlesuits, and the Twin Lance operating under the Retaliation Cadre, this is a wall-to-wall battlesuit army that rewards aggressive close-range positioning. The win condition is closing into the 8" bubble where the detachment's AP bonus kicks in, then unloading devastatingly improved firepower into high-value targets — Pathfinders mark priority threats while Coldstars reposition for multi-turn kill chains. It punishes heavy-armour lists severely, with improved Strength and AP at close range creating anti-tank overload that even durable targets struggle to absorb across multiple angles. It cracks open against armies that can deny the 8" window through deep strike denial, strong screening, or alpha-striking the battlesuit blocks before they collapse into effective range.
599: Built around Neurolictors, Lictors, Broodlords, Genestealers, Von Ryan's Leapers, Raveners, Hyperadapted Raveners, Hormagaunts, Deathleaper, Neurotyrant, Zoanthropes, and Biovores, this is a deep-strike-heavy infiltration swarm that floods the board from every angle with threats that appear exactly where they hurt most. The engine is character assassination and objective saturation simultaneously — Lictors and Neurolictors drop in with hit-reroll access against Characters, Broodlords and Genestealer blobs slam into priority targets, and Biovores chip away at screens to open lanes for the melee wave. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't contest every zone, drowning them in activations and forcing impossible priority decisions across multiple dangerous units. Against heavy shooting lists with wide screens and durable midfield presence, the fragility of the smaller infiltrating units gets exposed before they can land their punches.
515: Built around biovores, maleceptors, tyrannofexes, exocrines, genestealers, hormagaunts, a broodlord, neurotyrant, hive tyrant, norn emissary, and lictors, Invasion Fleet fields a genuinely wide toolkit — heavy shooting platforms backed by screening chaff and a sharp melee strike force. The plan is to select a Hyper-adaptation turn one that matches the matchup, then leverage the maleceptor-neurotyrant synapse network to push big shooting from exocrines and tyrannofexes while genestealers and hormagaunts contest and punish overextension in melee. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't absorb multi-vector pressure simultaneously — the horde screens while the gunline deletes, and genestealer units threaten lethal charges if opponents pull back to avoid the shooting. The breadth that makes it flexible is also its liability: there's no single dominant threat multiplier, so a tight, focused list can identify and isolate its most dangerous elements and trade efficiently before the adaptation advantage compounds.
612: Built around Slaughterbound, Eightbound, Exalted Eightbound, the Daemon Prince of Khorne, and Jakhals screening the advance, this list runs the Possessed Slaughterband detachment to give every Possessed unit Brazen Fury — surging up to D6" after taking shooting casualties — and pairs it with Vessels of Wrath to punch characters up with Cleave or improved AP on the fight. The win condition is a relentless mid-table brawl: use Jakhals to hold early objectives and absorb fire while the Possessed wave surges forward, then crash Eightbound and Slaughterbound into the enemy's scoring units and grind them off the board. Shooting-heavy lists that expect to whittle down the approach actually accelerate the Possessed surge, and the sheer volume of high-AP melee punishes light-infantry armies that can't win a prolonged fight. The build cracks against hard alpha-strike lists or elite melee that can delete key units before Brazen Fury fires, and it has limited answers to dug-in vehicles at range unless the minority Forgefiend picks are included.
708: Built around Allarus Custodians, Vertus Praetors, Custodian Guard, a Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator Armour, a Blade Champion, and Witchseekers, this is a transported infantry brawler that floods the midboard with elite bodies across multiple unit types. The win condition is physical board domination — crashing Allarus and the Shield-Captain into priority targets via ingress-into-charge sequences while Vertus Praetors and Guard lock down objectives and Witchseekers screen out cheap chaff. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies that cannot contest multiple midboard threats simultaneously, as individually tough Custodes units force opponents to overcommit resources to clear each one. However, it cracks against high-volume shooting lists that can strip key units below effective fighting strength before the brawl begins, neutralizing the close-range pressure that the entire engine depends on.
723: Built around Sydonian Dragoons with taser lances, Ironstrider Ballistarii, Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, Sicarian Infiltrators, and Onager Dunecrawlers, this is a layered skimmer-and-infantry hybrid running predominantly Lords of the Forge, which grants Tech-Priests solid survivability and the Baffling Data Screed ability to force enemy vehicles into reactive saves. The plan is to pressure mid-table with Dragoons crashing into anything soft while Ballistarii and Dunecrawlers sustain a heavy gunline behind screens of Rangers and Infiltrators, converting board control into primary scoring. It punishes mechanised armies hardest — Baffling Data Screed taxes opposing vehicles, and the Dragoons' taser lances shred anything that wanders into charge range without sufficient anti-melee screening. Dense elite infantry with high invulnerable saves cracks it open, as the layered lethality relies on volume rather than precision anti-armour, leaving it exposed when it can't out-trade on activations.
492: Built around Allarus Custodians, Blade Champion, Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, Vertus Praetors, Venatari Custodians, and a Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator armour, supported by Witchseekers and Caladius Grav-Tanks, this is a multi-wave melee-and-shoot hybrid that floods the midboard with elite, durable infantry. The plan is to use the Shield Host's Martial Ka'tah cycling — fishing for Critical Hits on 5s or sharpening Armour Penetration — to extract maximum value from repeated close-range brawls while Tharanatoi Hammerblow ingress-charges Terminators into backfield threats turn after turn. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that can't absorb the attrition of tough Custodes bodies contesting every midboard objective simultaneously. It cracks open against mass high-volume shooting that overwhelms even T5–T6 saves before the melee engine can engage.
439: Built around Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, Hastarii Fusiliers, Skitarii Rangers, Vanguard, and Sicarian Infiltrators riding Skorpius Duneriders, this is a mobile gunline that floods the board with layered shooting from infantry packed into transports and disgorged at optimal range. The win condition is stacking overlapping fire lanes — Manipulus buffing Hastarii and Rangers while Marshals keep units fighting — to delete priority targets before the opponent can consolidate, with Ironstrider Ballistarii providing medium-range fire support from the flanks. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't absorb the sheer volume of accurate, layered fire across multiple units simultaneously. It cracks under sustained melee pressure from fast assault forces that can reach the transports early, stripping the mobility that lets the gunline choose its engagement range.
741: Built around Tempestus Scions, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Scout Sentinels, Gaunt's Ghosts, Cadian Shock Troops, Cadian Command Squads, Krieg Combat Engineers, and Kasrkin, this is a mass-infantry gunline that floods the board with cheap, skilled bodies across multiple unit types. The win condition is volume and redundancy — Command Squads stack Orders onto Scions and Kasrkin to amplify shooting output while Gaunt's Ghosts and Engineers contest and deny mid-board objectives, grinding opponents out of scoring positions. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't clear sheer unit volume efficiently, overwhelming them through attrition and objective saturation. It cracks open against armies with high-volume mortal wound output or powerful area-clearance tools that delete multiple infantry units per turn, since losing scoring bodies faster than Orders can compensate collapses the engine entirely.
461: Built around waves of Plaguebearers, Beasts of Nurgle, Great Unclean Ones, Rotigus, and supporting characters including Sloppity Bilepipers, Poxbringers, and Nurglings, this is a suffocating mid-board brawler running Plague Legion with Warptide as its mobility engine. The plan is to flood the midfield with durable Nurgle bodies, force Battle-shock tests on everything within 9" every Command phase, and grind opponents into the dirt through attrition while Plaguebearers — advancing and still eligible to charge via Warptide — contest and hold objectives deep into the game. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot efficiently clear cheap, resilient screens, as the layered durability of the horde simply outlasts their damage output while Battle-shock cascades degrade their ability to fight back. However, high-volume mid-strength shooting that ignores Battle-shock penalties or armies that can alpha-strike and eliminate the supporting characters early can collapse the buff network before the grind engine gets established.
586: Built around waves of Daemonettes, Fiends, Beasts of Nurgle, Keepers of Secrets, the Contorted Epitome, the Tormentbringer, and the Masque of Slaanesh, this list weaponises both Legion Of Excess and Warptide to create a perpetual-motion assault engine: Daemonettes advance and still charge, Fell Back units re-engage the same turn, and nothing ever truly disengages. The win condition is layered combat pressure across every zone simultaneously — flooding objectives with expendable Daemonette screens while Fiends and Keepers hunt anything that contests, making it nearly impossible to hold a safe position anywhere on the board. It punishes slow, castle-style armies brutally, as the advance-and-charge loop denies breathing room and lets the list trade efficiently into anything that tries to sit on objectives. The weakness is volume of quality anti-infantry fire before the first charge lands — a list that can thin Daemonettes at range disrupts the screen math and leaves flanks exposed to counterplay.
747: Built around War Dog Stalkers, Karnivores, and Brigands — six to eight fast, aggressive light Knights swarming the board with overlapping threat vectors. The plan is to pick apart opposing armies piece by piece using mobile anti-armour pressure across multiple activation windows, with Infernal Lance's Malefic Surge or Houndpack Lance's Sustained Hits 1 focus-fire funneling concentrated damage onto priority targets each turn. The sheer volume of durable, fast chassis punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot answer eight separate threat sources simultaneously, forcing unfavorable trades across the entire field. The build cracks under high-volume anti-tank lists that can efficiently strip individual War Dogs before they activate, since losing even two early collapses the activation economy the entire engine depends on.
750: Built around Cultist Mobs screening for Knight Abominants, Chaos Cerastus Knight Lancers, and Knight Despoilers, this Iconoclast Fiefdom warband pairs a dense infantry base with a flexible roster of hulking war engines. The cultists flood midfield objectives while the Knights hunt priority targets, with the Iconoclast Fiefdom rule allowing DAMNED units — cultists, and in some lists Traitor Guardsmen or Nurglings — to reinforce the screen and contest boards states that pure Knight lists cannot hold. It punishes slower, elite armies that cannot simultaneously clear chaff and trade into multiple heavy targets, forcing opponents into lose-lose removal decisions across the entire board. The build cracks open against high-volume mortal wound output or mass anti-tank that can strip Knights before the screen thins, and lists lacking objective control muscle from the Knight Characters can be outscored by faster, more numerous armies.
727:
Built around Chaos Terminator squads, Cultist Mob screens, Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Mutilators, Kravek Morne, and Defilers, this list runs the Cabal of Chaos detachment — with most lists adding Warpstrike Champions as a second detachment for end-of-turn repositioning of Terminators, Obliterators, and Mutilators off the board.

The engine is Dark Pact synergy: Psyker Sorcerers boost their ranged attacks with +1 Strength when they Pact, while the Warpstrike Champions rule lets Terminators and Mutilators teleport back in at optimal angles each turn, threatening contested mid-board objectives repeatedly rather than committing once.

This punishes static gunlines hard — the redeployment loop means holding midfield against this list demands constant attention, and screens of Cultists make it difficult to suppress the Terminator threat before it resets.

Its weakness is high-volume mortal wounds or overwatch-style alpha strikes that delete Terminators before they can redeploy, and elite melee lists that can tie up the Cultist screens efficiently and prevent the Warpstrike repositioning from firing safely.
729: Built around Chaos Bikers, Cultist Mobs, Traitor Guardsmen, Defilers, and Chaos Rhinos operating under Pactbound Zealots, this list floods the board with cheap bodies while parking Daemon Engine firepower at range. The plan is to drown opponents in screening chaff — Cultists and Guardsmen holding flanks and objectives — while Defilers and Bikers threaten mobile anti-armour pressure and melee aggression backed by Lethal Hits on 5+ in combat. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that struggle to clear waves of expendable infantry before the Daemon Engines grind them down. However, it cracks under high-volume mortal wound output or strong anti-horde shooting that strips the chaff screens efficiently, leaving the heavier engines exposed and unsupported mid-table.
725: Built around Ravenwing Command Squads, Ravenwing Black Knights, Outriders, Land Speeder Vengances, Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, Sammael, Azrael, Scout Squads, and Invader ATVs, this is an all-mounted Dark Angels force running Company Of Hunters — a detachment granting every Adeptus Astartes unit [ASSAULT] on ranged attacks, and letting MOUNTED units advance-and-shoot freely, while Darkflight Pursuit layers [IGNORES COVER] onto Ravenwing FLY units in nearly three-quarters of lists. The plan is relentless board-wide pressure: advance every turn, shoot without penalty, contest objectives from turn one, and pour mobile anti-armour fire — Thunderstrikes, Vengances, ATVs — into anything that tries to hold ground. It punishes static gunlines and castled elite armies that rely on cover saves and positioning discipline, overwhelming them with advance-shoot volume before they can set up. It cracks against fast melee armies that can tag multiple units simultaneously, since even fall-back-and-shoot capability struggles when the entire fleet is locked in close combat at once.
637: Built around multiple Land Speeder Vengeances, Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, and the leadership of Azrael and Lion El'Jonson, this Dark Angels force floods the board with fast-moving skimmer firepower. The plan is to exploit the Fulguris Task Force's first-turn ingress move — available in lists running that detachment — to push Speeder units immediately into optimal firing lanes, applying sustained anti-armour pressure while Scouts and Intercessors hold objectives. It punishes mechanised and armour-heavy lists through mobile anti-tank overload, making it difficult for an opponent to screen or reposition vehicles out of threat range. Armies that can strip skimmers at range or deny early board positioning with aggressive deep strike threats will crack the relatively fragile hull count before it can leverage its mobility advantage.
642: Built around Deathwing Knights, Chaplains in Terminator Armour, Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, and Inner Circle Companions, this is a dense terminator-hammer list split across Interrogation Conclave and Wrath of the Rock detachments depending on the pilot. The win condition is crashing an elite melee wall into mid-board, using Chaplain kill-triggers to chain battle-shock across enemy units while Azrael and the Lion amplify the terminator core's staying power. Wrath of the Rock's wound-roll penalty makes the armoured infantry punishing to crack for high-Strength, low-volume anti-tank shooting, rewarding attrition against gunlines that can't flood attacks. The build struggles against mass-wound horde lists and skimmer-heavy armies that can avoid the melee engagement entirely, exploiting the list's low model count and limited ranged reach.
726: Built around Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and a dense Ravenwing cavalry core of the Command Squad, Sammael, Black Knights, and Outriders, this is Wrath of the Rock's signature durability-and-pressure list. The engine is straightforward but punishing: Wrath of the Rock's wound-roll penalty on over-Strength attacks makes the entire Adeptus Astartes Infantry and Mounted battleline dramatically harder to kill, letting the cavalry screen and contest while the Deathwing hammer units crack open whatever survives the attrition. It excels against armies relying on high-Strength, moderate-volume shooting — the wound subtraction bleeds efficiency from anti-tank profiles trying to clear mid-Toughness bodies. Lists with massed low-Strength, high-volume fire that stays at or under the target's Toughness entirely bypass the detachment's protection and can strip screens faster than the melee core can respond.
636: Built around Land Speeders, Land Speeder Vengances, Inner Circle Companions, and Librarians operating under the Librarius Conclave detachment, this list floods the board with fast-moving skimmers and elite infantry backed by Azrael and Sternguard Veterans. The engine is the Librarius Conclave's rotating Psychic Discipline — Divination's re-rolls amplify the skimmer swarm's volume fire to strip vehicles, while Biomancy pushes Companions and Scouts into aggressive board position to control objectives and deny space. It punishes static gunlines and low-mobility armies hard, overwhelming them with maneuvering threats from multiple angles that are nearly impossible to prioritize correctly. However, dedicated anti-infantry saturation and armies that can isolate and delete the Companions before they engage will crack the list open, since the mobile scoring core is fragile once the fast screens are peeled away.
629: Built around Deathshroud Terminators, Lords of Contagion, a Lord of Virulence, Blightlord Terminators, Typhus, and Poxwalker screens, with Myphitic Blight-Haulers providing mobile threat saturation, this list runs the Death Lord's Chosen detachment to stack Contagion pressure across every phase. The win condition is attrition through the Death Lord's Chosen passive — rolling against every Afflicted enemy unit each Command phase to drain mortal wounds across the board while Characters extended by Paragons of Putrescence spread Contagion Range up to 12", keeping the whole army inside the bleed zone simultaneously. It punishes mid-range elite armies that cluster tightly and stay Afflicted, where the mortal wound engine fires repeatedly against multiple valuable units without the opponent being able to disengage cleanly. It cracks under pressure from fast, objective-dominant lists that can strip Contagion targets before the passive fires and outmaneuver the slow, foot-slogging core before the attrition math catches up.
628: Built around Myphitic Blight-Haulers, Poxwalkers, Deathshroud Terminators, Plague Marines, Typhus, a Lord of Contagion, Malignant Plaguecasters, Foetid Bloat-Drones, Biologus Putrifier, and Chaos Spawn under the Paragons Of Putrescence detachment, which extends Death Guard Character Contagion Range by 3", this list is a slow-rolling plague engine that layers debuff auras across the entire board before combat is even joined. The win condition is Contagion saturation — Characters push their extended auras over objectives and screens, letting Deathshroud and Plague Marines delete whatever stumbles into range while Blight-Haulers provide mobile anti-armour pressure. It punishes gunline armies that can't disengage, as the Contagion bubble rewards standing and fighting — exactly what static lists do. What cracks it open is a fast alpha-strike that kills the Characters early, collapsing the aura network before it can blanket the midfield.
701: Built around Deathwatch Veterans, Deathwatch Terminators, dual Librarians, and Intercessor squads, this is a mid-table shooting and brawling force that leans on Firestorm Assault Force in most lists to give its ranged weapons Assault and a Strength bump inside 12", turning aggressive repositioning into raw killing power. The plan is to push Terminators and Veterans forward behind Intercessor screens, close to within 12" to trigger that Strength bonus, and leverage Librarian psychic disciplines — Divination for re-rolls or Biomancy for movement — to crack priority targets and score through raw attrition. It punishes horde armies and gunlines hard, since the combination of high model-count screens, massed bolter volume, and close-range Strength bonuses overloads light-save and medium-save targets efficiently. It struggles against fast elite armies that can bypass the screen, isolate Terminators before they close, and avoid that 12" killzone entirely.
744: Built around Daemon Princes of Slaanesh with Wings, Maulerfiends, Defilers, Lords Exultant, Infractors in Rhinos, Tormentors, Noise Marines, and Flawless Blades, this Coterie of the Conceited list drives a wall of mobile threat into the mid-board every turn. The win condition is the Pact points engine: pledge an achievable kill count each round, cash it in consistently, and weaponize the accumulating Pact points to amplify the army's already punishing melee and anti-armour output. It punishes slower gunline and armour-heavy lists that cannot thin the wave of Maulerfiends and Princes before they hit combat, and the transported Infractors deny opponents clean objective holds. Lists that can alpha-strike the Princes and Maulerfiends off the board early disrupt the pledge math, leaving the slower infantry elements stranded without their kill-generating vanguard.
746: Built around Lords Exultant buffing waves of Infractors and Tormentors delivered by Chaos Rhinos, backed by Maulerfiends, Defilers, Flawed Blades, and winged Daemon Princes hunting flanks. Peerless Bladesmen turns every post-charge fight into a choice of Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1, while Spectacle of Slaughter gives Flawless Blades Fights First, letting the list dictate the close-combat exchange at every angle and grind opponents off objectives through sheer melee volume. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't absorb multiple simultaneous charge threats across the midboard, since the transport-delivered infantry wave and roaming monsters force unfavorable trades on multiple fronts at once. It cracks against armies with robust screen-and-deny packages or strong overwatch equivalents that can strip the Rhinos before they deliver their payload, removing the charge trigger that makes Peerless Bladesmen fire.
743: Built around Flawless Blades, Noise Marines, Tormentors, Lord Kakophonists, and a winged Daemon Prince, this list runs the Spectacle of Slaughter detachment to give Flawless Blades Fights First, then ferries the bulk of its infantry forward in Chaos Rhinos to hit the midboard as a coordinated melee wave. The win condition is crashing charge-enabled units into contested objectives — Peerless Bladesmen rewards charging units with Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1, so the list scores by winning fights, holding ground, and denying the opponent's ability to trade efficiently. It punishes slower combat armies and horde infantry that can't survive Fights First pressure backed by high-volume melee output. It struggles against gunlines and alpha-strike lists that strip the Rhino transports before the charge lands, leaving the melee core exposed and reactive.
572: Built around Purestrain Genestealers, Aberrants, and their Abominant leaders amplified by Biosanctic Broodsurge, this is a mass-horde assault army that throws waves of charging bodies into the midboard and tears opponents apart in melee. The engine is charge-fueled: Biosanctic Broodsurge adds 1 to Charge rolls and stacks bonus Attacks onto Purestrains, Aberrants, and Biophagus units that charged, while Neophyte Hybrids in terrain regenerate 3 wounds per Command phase under Xenocult Masses to hold objectives behind the assault wave. It punishes slow, static gunlines that cannot thin the horde before contact — the sheer volume of bodies soaks shooting while the layered lethality of multiple charging elite units overwhelms focused defenders. Armies that can screen effectively, deny charges with deep strike denial, or blast chaff before the wave arrives expose its weakness: no charge, no bonus Attacks, no teeth.
754: Built around Nemesis Dreadknights, Paladin Squads, Interceptor Squads, Strike Squads, Brotherhood Terminators, and a Grand Master in Nemesis Dreadknight, this is a mobile melee pressure list running the Argent Assault detachment with Banishers as a frequent secondary purchase. The core engine is Paladin Squads punching through high-Toughness targets via the detachment's wound-roll bonus, while Interceptors and Dreadknights flood midfield early and the Banishers Leadership test layers on Sustained Hits 1 or equivalent to amplify the fight phase across the board. It punishes slow, durable armies that rely on Toughness as a defense, since Paladins strip that protection and Dreadknights apply relentless board-wide threat. Fast, high-volume shooting lists that can pick apart elite infantry before they close will crack this open, as the army is glass-jawed once its melee units are attrited in transit.
753: Built around Castellan Crowe, multiple Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Purifier Squads, Strike Squads, and Brotherhood Terminators, this Warpbane Task Force list uses Purifier positioning to physically extend Hallowed Ground across the midboard, layering objective control with a mobile elite infantry core. The win condition is map domination through Hallowed Ground saturation — Purifiers push into No Man's Land to unlock additional detachment benefits while Dreadknights provide fast-moving anti-armour punch and Crowe enables Purifier synergies. It punishes slow or static armies that cannot contest multiple midfield objectives simultaneously, as the combined threat range of Dreadknights and Terminators forces an opponent to defend everywhere at once. Highly mobile elite forces that can collapse individual Purifier squads — breaking Hallowed Ground coverage — and armies with sufficient long-range firepower to strip Dreadknights before they engage will crack this list open.
740: Built around Deathwatch Kill Teams, Imperial Navy Breachers, Watch Masters, Subductor Squads, Aquila Kill Teams, and a dense support staff of Inquisitors, Navigators, Sanctifiers, and Rogue Trader Entourages under the Imperialis Fleet detachment, this list fields an extraordinary volume of cheap-to-mid infantry across every inch of the board. The engine is Imperialis Fleet's Eliminate At All Costs focus-fire directive, stacking hit bonuses from multiple units onto a priority target each Command phase while a mass of bodies simultaneously contests every objective marker simultaneously. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally — the sheer unit density creates anti-alpha-strike resilience, and layered lethality from stacked gunline units overwhelms armies that cannot match the action-economy of fighting across a dozen units simultaneously. Its weakness is volume-of-attacks armies and anything with blast weapons or mortal wound output, since the wall of cheap infantry that defines the list collapses quickly when the opponent can punish mass-horde clustering with area-damage tools.
756: Built around multiple Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Purgation Squads, Purifier Squads, and Castellan Crowe, this list runs either Fires of Purgation or Warpbane Task Force to layer psychic shooting pressure across the board. The plan is to pin enemy units with Righteous Persecution, forcing battle-shock rolls at -1, while Dreadknights threaten mobile anti-armour and Purifiers extend Hallowed Ground to contest mid-table objectives under favorable conditions. It punishes horde-heavy armies hardest, where massed psychic firepower and battle-shock cascades can strip bodies and deny actions simultaneously. It cracks open against elite low-model-count armies that shrug off battle-shock and can surgically remove Purgation Squads before the pinning engine comes online.
761: Built around Armiger Helverins, Armiger Warglaives, and Knight Crusaders, this list pairs a wall of Armigers with a heavy Knight centerpiece and leans into the Throne-Bonded Outriders detachment's core payoff: every Armiger benefiting from a Bondsman ability fires its ranged weapons with Ignores Cover. The Valourstrike Lance then lets the whole army Advance and still shoot without penalty, turning mobility into offense — the kill chain is advance into range, trigger Bondsman, and pour Ignores Cover shooting into whatever the opponent tried to hide. This punishes gunlines and armies relying on terrain and obscuring to keep elite or vehicle targets alive, as cover saves simply stop functioning against the activated Armigers. The list cracks when opponents can close quickly and force melee engagements or strip Knights before Bondsman abilities come online, since the army has almost no redundant bodies to absorb early losses.
522: Built around near-universal Cthonian Berserk squads (almost four on average) supported by Berehk Stornbröw, Ûthar the Destined, Einhyr Hearthguard, and Hekaton Land Fortresses, this list uses the Dêlve Assault Shift detachment to give every Berserk unit Deep Strike, flooding midfield with melee infantry from unexpected angles while Hernkyn Pioneers and Yaegirs hold ground and Kapricus Carriers move the fight. The win condition is simultaneous pressure across multiple board quadrants — drop Beserks into threat range turn one, force your opponent into reactive positioning, then grind them off objectives with layered melee and supporting gunline fire. It punishes slow, static armies that cannot reposition fast enough to handle four independent Deep Strike threats appearing in their deployment edge. Elite low-model armies that delete Berserk squads wholesale before they swing, or lists with strong screen-and-deny coverage that can absorb the drops without cracking open, will consistently deflate the threat before the melee engine fires.
579: Built around Doomsday Arks, Canoptek Wraiths, Skorpekh Lords and Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Flayed Ones, Hexmark Destroyers, Imotekh, Canoptek Reanimators, and Technomancers operating under Awakened Dynasty's +1 to Hit for CHARACTER-led units, this is a highly mobile toolbox army that floods the board with fast, resilient threats across every phase. The win condition is multi-vector pressure — Wraiths and Ophydians contest midfield while Destroyers hunt priority targets with character-boosted accuracy, Doomsday Arks crack armour at range, and Flayed Ones punish overextension. It excels against slower, static armies that struggle to handle simultaneous threats arriving from multiple angles before they can be prioritised and eliminated. However, high-volume mortal wound output or elite melee that bypasses reanimation can dismantle the layered durability, and a true alpha strike that removes the CHARACTER leaders collapses the hit-bonus engine before it fires.
739: Built around Lokhust Lords leading Lokhust Destroyers in Awakened Dynasty, with Ophydian Destroyers, Skorpekh engines, Canoptek Wraiths, and C'tan Shards rounding out a deep roster of independent threats, this list plays as a swarm of elite, self-sufficient kill elements rather than a single deathstar. The Awakened Dynasty's +1 to Hit while a Character leads makes every Lokhust Destroyer unit a precision strike package, and Veil of Darkness on key characters lets the build reposition threats mid-game to hunt priority targets and seize scoring lanes. It punishes static gunlines and fragile elite armies that can't handle multiple simultaneous high-damage vectors across the table. Lists with dense chaff screens and strong counter-punch in melee can strip the supporting Characters, collapsing the Hit bonus and leaving Destroyer units underperforming when they need it most.
767: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, massed Boyz squads, Painboyz, Warbosses, and Wazdakka Gutsmek flooding the midboard, this list runs dual detachments — Equatorial Hordes to Scout 6" up to three MOB/KOMMANDOS units and Freebooter Krew to generate a rotating loot objective while granting Sustained Hits 1 to every Orks Infantry, Mounted, and Walker attack made near or on that objective. The win condition is suffocating the midboard with sheer volume: bodies, Sustained Hits 1 triggers, and Painboy durability let it grind through scoring while Kommandos pressure backfield objectives. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies that can't match the attrition or answer multiple simultaneous threats across the board. Armies with strong blast weapons, high-volume mortal wound output, or elite melee that can isolate and delete Boyz mobs before Painboyz stabilize them will crack the engine apart.
557: Built around Beast Snagga Boyz, Beastboss characters, Squighog Boyz, Boyz, Gretchin screens, Kill Rig, Ghazghkull Thraka, Mozrog Skragbad, Painboy support, and Kommandos, this is a thundering green tide that floods the midboard with expendable bodies and hard-hitting Beast Snagga units. The plan is to plant multiple massive infantry blobs on objectives while Squighog Boyz and Ghazghkull punch through whatever is holding them, generating pressure across every lane simultaneously. It punishes elite low-model armies badly — those opponents simply cannot kill enough models fast enough to deny board control before the Orks crush them in melee. Tightly packed, high-damage shooting armies that can thin the horde before contact, combined with anti-horde area denial, are the primary threat, as losing model count early collapses the combat weight the list depends on.
683: Built around Intercessor Squads, Heavy Intercessors, and multiple Librarians running Bastion Task Force, this is a dense infantry gunline that blankets the board with Battleline bodies and psychic support. The engine is the detachment's core ability: Battleline units that Advance or Fall Back remain eligible to shoot, charge, and perform Actions, letting the army score objectives aggressively while maintaining a withering volume of fire — Librarians cycling Divination or Biomancy each round to tune output on the fly. It punishes mid-range brawler armies and objective-racing lists that expect to outmaneuver infantry blobs, since there is no safe window to force trade-offs between holding ground and fighting back. The list cracks open against elite anti-infantry overload or high-damage alpha strikes that can delete key Battleline units before the shoot-and-advance loop gets rolling.
554: Built around Kayvaan Shrike, Aethon Shaan, and a dense core of Jump Pack Assault Intercessors, Vanguard Veterans, and Inceptors, this list operates under Shadowmark Talon, which blankets every Adeptus Astartes unit in cover against any attacker beyond 12" — making the entire army remarkably durable at range. The plan is to exploit that passive durability to tempo aggressively: Shaan's Unparalleled Tactician ability fires the Into Darkness Stratagem for free once per round, enabling sustained deep-strike pressure while Centurion Devastators anchor a heavy gunline that punishes anything forced to close in. Opposing lists that rely on mid-to-long-range shooting to clear infantry are severely punished, as the cover rule strips their efficiency while Jump Pack units and Inceptors swarm objectives and apply mobile anti-armour. Armies that can flood within 12" to negate the cover bubble — or that alpha-strike the Centurions off the board before they can fire — expose how fragile this build's long-range damage engine actually is.
760: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Terminator Assault Squad, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, and Arjac Rockfist, this is a transport-heavy terminator hammer that floods the mid-table with armoured bodies. The win condition is delivering multiple terminator squads into melee through transports while Saga of the Great Wolf's rotating Hunting Packs — chiefly Encircling Jaws for re-rolled charges — guarantee the contact that turns elite infantry into scrap. It punishes lists that rely on expensive characters, monsters, or vehicles, since Saga of the Beastslayer arms the entire force with Lethal Hits against those target types, turning every swing into a deletion event. Lists that can screen the mid-table aggressively, deny transport lanes, or flood the board with cheap wounds stretch the terminator brick thin and exploit its low model count.
759: Built around Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, a deep stack of Wolf Guard Terminators anchored by Arjac Rockfist, and a Captain in Terminator Armour, this is a Saga of the Great Wolf elite-melee hammer that buries opponents under multi-squad terminator waves. The win condition is delivering two or more Terminator units into the enemy mid-table in the same turn — often via Land Raider Redeemer transport — using Saga's rotating Hunting Pack buffs like Encircling Jaws to guarantee charges out of disembark or advance. It punishes mobile, low-armour hordes and toolbox armies that lack the anti-tank volume to simultaneously threaten the Redeemer, Bjorn, and multiple Terminator blobs. Elite gunlines with high-AP, multi-damage shooting that can pick apart the terminator wave before it arrives, or armies that can out-range and kite the delivery system, will crack this list open before it closes distance.
773: Built around Tzaangor Enlightened, Sekhetar Robots, Scarab Occult Terminators, Rubric Marines, Defilers, and Daemon Princes supported by Sorcerers in Terminator armour, this is a mass-horde psyker army that floods the board with layered threats across every range band. The win condition is board saturation — Tzaangor Enlightened swarm objectives and tie up midfield while Sekhetar Robots and Terminators grind through anything that tries to hold ground, with Sorcerers keeping the psychic engine running to fuel rituals and buff chains. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't answer volume, trading efficiently through sheer unit count and layered lethality that forces opponents into impossible priority decisions. It cracks under concentrated high-AP, high-damage shooting that can delete whole squads before the swarm closes — armies that can alpha-strike the Terminators and Daemon Princes off the board early remove the hard-hitting anchors the horde needs to actually convert pressure into kills.
771: Built around Sorcerers in Terminator Armour leading Scarab Occult Terminators, waves of Sekhetar Robots, Rubric Marines as durable objective holders, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows flooding the midfield, and Magnus the Red as the list's apex threat, this is a mass-horde army with a hard elite fist buried inside it. The win condition is layered board saturation — Enlightened and Robots contest and contest again while the Scarab Terminator hammer delivers psychic firepower into whatever the opponent commits to clearing the chaff. It punishes lists that can't multi-task: armies built to delete elite targets get buried in bodies, while those that focus on chaff removal get cracked by the Terminators and Magnus arriving with full threat. Weak to fast, high-volume mortal-wound output or anti-horde area denial that can thin the screening layer and isolate the hammers before they engage.
772: Built around Magnus the Red, a winged Daemon Prince, Scarab Occult Terminators, and waves of Rubric Marines, Tzaangors, and Tzaangor Enlightened, this Grand Coven list plays a towering psychic horde that floods the board with bodies while its elite core delivers concentrated ranged Psychic firepower. The engine is Grand Coven's rotational ability — cycling Imbued Manifestation to extend Psychic weapon ranges and Psychic Maelstrom when it's time to spike damage — letting Magnus and the Terminators project lethal threat well beyond normal engagement distances while cheap chaff holds objectives. It punishes mid-range shooting armies by outranging them on Psychic weapons and drowning their threat assessment in sheer unit count, forcing impossible priority choices across Tzaangors, Chaos Spawn, and Sekhetar Robots simultaneously. Aggressive melee alpha-strikes that can reach Magnus before he cycles his buffs, or mass mortal-wound output that bypasses the horde's durability layers, will crack this list open fastest.
774: Built around Defilers, Forgefiends, Sekhetar Robots, a winged Daemon Prince, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, and half the time Magnus the Red, this is a Hexwarp Thrallband list that floods the board with Daemon Engines and Psychic-tagged melee threats. The win condition is controlling No Man's Land objectives to extend the Flow of Magic across the midfield, then leveraging the Sekhetar Cohort's +1 WS aura from nearby Psykers to crash boosted Sekhetar Robots into whatever the Forgefiends and Enlightened have already softened at range. It punishes mid-density armoured lists badly, stacking mobile anti-tank from multiple angles while the layered Psychic shooting strips screens before the melee wave arrives. Armies that can deny its midfield objective control early collapse the Flow of Magic engine, and elite hordes with strong alpha-strike capability can gut the Daemon Engines before the aura synergy goes online.
780: Built around Magnus the Red, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Sorcerers, and Chaos Spawn screening in mass numbers, this Grand Coven list uses the detachment's rotating Command phase abilities — including extended Psychic weapon range and enhanced Psychic shooting — to project overwhelming firepower while flooding the board with bodies. The win condition is layering Psychic shooting from Magnus and Rubric Marines behind a thick Chaos Spawn and Tzaangor screen, using mobile pieces like the winged Daemon Prince and Exalted Sorcerer on Disc to threaten flanks and pressure secondaries. It punishes static gunlines that struggle to chew through horde bodies before the Psychic payoff units get range-extended and into position. It cracks open against elite melee armies that can punch through the screen cleanly and close into Magnus before the Psychic abilities cycle through their one-per-battle uses.
611: Built around Khorne Berzerkers, Exalted Eightbound, Eightbound, Slaughterbound, and Angron — all supercharged by the Berzerker Warband detachment's charge bonus adding +1 Attack and +2 Strength to every melee weapon after a charge — this list floods the midboard with bodies transported in Chaos Rhinos, screened by Jakhals and Chaos Spawn, and crashing into targets with Khârn the Betrayer amplifying the kill chain. The win condition is converting charge-buffed melee weight into rapid unit destruction, snowballing board control through raw combat output rather than passive holding. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot absorb repeated charge-boosted strikes across multiple units simultaneously. It cracks open when it faces shooting-heavy lists that peel transports early, strip screens before the charge lands, or deny the charge entirely — leaving expensive melee infantry stranded without the activation that makes them dangerous.
792: Built around Corsair Voidscarred, Prince Yriel, Corsair Voidreavers, Corsair Skyreavers, Warp Spiders, Striking Scorpions, Lhykhis, Rangers, Shroud Runners, and the Avatar of Khaine, this Eldritch Raiders list weaponizes the detachment's core rule — Anhrathe, Rangers, and Shroud Runners units can Advance and still charge — to flood the board with fast, multi-layered lethal threats from turn one. The win condition is momentum: advance screens and flankers into scoring positions while the Avatar and Voidscarred punch into priority targets, creating kill chains the opponent can't fully address in a single turn. It punishes slower, static armies that can't reposition to meet simultaneous threats from multiple angles, with layered Lethal Hits across the roster amplifying damage output even on glancing attacks. Its weakness is concentrated firepower — elite shooting lists that can delete key pieces before the advance-charge engine engages leave it exposed, and losing Prince Yriel early strips the leadership glue that keeps the assault coherent.
789: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs led by Lemartes, Sanguinary Priests, and a supporting core of Assault Intercessors and Bladeguard Veterans, this list runs primarily under the Liberator Assault Group detachment, which adds 2 Strength and 1 Attack to all melee weapons on any unit that charged that turn. The plan is to deliver multiple elite melee threats simultaneously — Priests buffing durability and fight-back, Lemartes supercharging Death Company, and charged Sanguinary Guard hitting at boosted stats — while Baal Predators and Intercessors hold ground and apply fire support. It punishes medium-armour infantry lists that can't absorb multiple high-Strength charging units across several fronts at once. Opponents who screen effectively to deny charges, or who pack enough anti-infantry firepower to strip the jump pack units before they land, can dismantle the engine before it swings.
788: Built around Vindicators, Sanguinary Guard, Commander Dante, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, and a Captain with Jump Pack, this list pairs hard-hitting jump infantry with heavy demolisher cannon fire across multiple detachment flavors — Rage-Cursed Onslaught, Stormlance Task Force, or Legacy of Grace. The win condition is coordinated threat overload: Vindicators crack armour and clear screens while Sanguinary Guard and Death Company crash in with charge-boosted attack stacks, generating kills that translate into board control and primary points. It punishes slower gunlines and low-model-count elite armies that can't absorb simultaneous vehicle fire and melee pressure from multiple angles. It cracks against fast, durable counter-charge lists that can absorb or redirect the initial assault wave and leave the Vindicators stranded without melee support.
643: Built around Terminator Assault Squads led by a Chaplain in Terminator Armour, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Sanguinary Guard, and screening Scouts, this is a multi-wave melee assault list running Rage-Cursed Onslaught. The engine is charge-stacking: every charging Adeptus Astartes unit gains +1 Attack on all melee weapons (or +2 if Battle-shocked), with re-rolls to wound on 1s baked in, letting multiple independent threat vectors crash into opposing lines simultaneously and overwhelm on raw volume. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that lack the bodies to absorb repeated high-Attack charges from both ground-pounding Terminators and airborne Death Company in the same turn. It cracks against defensive gunlines with strong overwatch, deep screen layers, or movement denial that prevent charges from landing cleanly, leaving expensive units exposed and underperforming.
791: Built around Death Company Dreadnoughts, Death Company Marines with jump packs, Sanguinary Guard, Lemartes, a jump pack Captain, Intercessors, and Commander Dante, this is a flying melee sledgehammer that exploits charge-triggered attack bonuses — either re-rolling wound rolls of 1 with extra attacks on the charge, or piling on Strength and Attacks simultaneously depending on detachment — to delete priority targets in a single activation. The win condition is using Lemartes to supercharge Death Company Marines into catastrophic charge turns while Sanguinary Guard and Dreadnoughts simultaneously threaten multiple flanks, overwhelming opponents who can only answer one assault vector at a time. It punishes slower melee armies and low-model-count elite lists that cannot screen charge lanes or trade attrition across multiple fronts. It cracks open against heavy shooting armies that can strip the jump pack units mid-approach before the charge lands, neutering the entire attack-bonus engine before it fires.
540: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Captains with Jump Packs, Sanguinary Priests, and nearly two Vindicators on average, this is a Angelic Inheritors list that pairs elite jump-pack assault elements with heavy demolisher cannon fire to crack armour and clear midfield simultaneously. The Vindicators anchor a punishing gunline while the Sanguinary Guard and Captains threaten aggressive repositioning, with Sanguinary Grace letting key Characters fall back and still shoot or charge to maintain relentless pressure on objectives. It punishes slow, armour-heavy lists by overloading them with mobile anti-tank angles from multiple vectors — jump infantry threatening flanks while Vindicator fire strips vehicles from range. Dedicated fast armies or deep-strike heavy threats can outpace the infantry screen, leaving Vindicators exposed and the jump pack elements stranded without targets to chain into.
648:
Built around Huron Blackheart, Chosen, Defilers, Warp Talons, and cheap horde bodies — Cultist Mobs, Red Corsairs Raiders, and Masters of the Maelstrom — this list runs two detachments simultaneously: Murdertalon Raiders and Veterans of the Long War.

The plan is to flood the board with expendable chaff to pressure objectives while Huron's Veterans of the Long War Focus of Hatred re-rolls stack onto a priority target, and Murdertalon Raiders' flying infantry punish anything already battle-shocked or half-strength with hit-roll re-rolls while becoming harder to kill in return.

It punishes low-model-count elite armies that struggle to trade efficiently into a deep horde, where the hit-penalty mechanic on wounded or shocked units compounds attrition beautifully.
