Dense, high-volume shooting lists that never trigger the half-strength or battle-shock thresholds neutralize both detachment payoffs entirely, leaving the army leaning on Defilers and Chosen alone to carry damage output.
785: Built around Rotigus, Deathshroud Terminators, a Lord of Contagion, and waves of Beasts of Nurgle, Nurglings, Poxwalkers, Plaguebearers, and Chaos Spawn, this Tallyband Summoners list exploits the detachment's core synergy: Plague Legions daemons sitting within 7" of Death Guard units gain Nurgle's Gift, while Death Guard within 7" of those daemons extend their Contagion Range by 3", creating an interlocking web of attrition across the entire midboard. The win condition is drowning opponents under layered lethality — stacking Contagion Range bubbles to corrode enemy durability while bodies flood objectives and Deathshroud punch out anything that survives the grind. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot trade efficiently against the sheer volume of durable wounds and cannot escape the expanding contagion aura. Concentrated high-damage shooting or alpha-strike lists that delete key synergy pieces before the web forms can unravel the whole engine before it gets going.
782: Built around Mortarion, Deathshroud Terminators, a Daemon Prince of Nurgle, Foetid Bloat-Drones, and a deep roster of supporting characters running Virulent Vectorium, this list plants Poxwalkers and Chaos Spawn on objectives to trigger the detachment's Afflicted condition while a slow-rolling wall of elite infantry and Defilers grinds forward. The win condition is suffocation: lock down objectives early to Afflict anything that contests them, then use Mortarion and Deathshroud as a hammer to dismantle whatever the opponent commits to clear your screening units. It absolutely punishes gunline armies that need to hold static firing positions, because those units spend most of the game Afflicted while being worn down by heavy blight launchers and Defiler firepower. The critical weakness is speed — a fast, deep-striking or hyper-mobile opponent can bypass the screen entirely, flip objectives before Afflicted triggers, and race ahead on secondaries before the slow Death Guard centre can respond.
768: Built around Squighog Boyz, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Ghazghkull Thraka, and Beast Snagga Boyz, all ferried forward in Trukks behind waves of Gretchin and Boyz screens, this is a Freebooter Krew horde that converts raw mass into mid-board control. The engine is the loot objective mechanic — designating a forward objective each Command phase and then flooding it with mounted and infantry bodies while the Squighog riders and Squigosaur bosses tear apart anything holding it. It punishes slow or fragile elite armies that cannot clear hordes efficiently, overwhelming them with layered threats across too many bodies to kill. It cracks when fast, high-AP shooting can strip the Trukks early and strand the assault payloads before they reach combat range.
794: Built around Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Arjac Rockfist, Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Guard Headtakers, and Vindicators operating under the Saga of the Great Wolf detachment, this list blends armoured firepower with elite melee infantry. The Vindicators supply mid-table anti-armour punch while the Terminators and Headtakers deliver transported shock assaults, cycling the Hunting Pack selections each Command phase to keep the entire force adaptable across the game's shifting demands. It punishes slower gunlines that struggle to screen against multi-vector threats, overloading them with Vindicator blasts and simultaneous melee pressure from Terminator bricks. Where it cracks is against hyper-mobile or deep-strike-heavy armies that can strip its infantry transports early, leaving the assault core exposed and unable to close without reliable re-roll support.
696: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Arjac Rockfist, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Ragnar Blackmane, Wulfen with Storm Shields, and Blood Claws flooding the board under the Saga of the Beastslayer detachment, which grants Lethal Hits to all Adeptus Astartes attacks made against Characters, Monsters, and Vehicles. The win condition is burying elite enemy units in a tide of Lethal Hits-enhanced melee, using Ragnar and Grimnar to push aggressive threats into mid-table brawls while Blood Claws and Intercessors hold objectives behind them. It punishes elite-heavy lists — particularly those leaning on Characters, Monsters, or Vehicles — because Lethal Hits dramatically amplifies efficiency against exactly those targets at every attack. It cracks against armies that can screen aggressively, deny the mid-table brawl, or strip its melee hitters before they engage, as the build has limited reach and no defensive recovery once its expensive infantry are bled out.
776: Built around Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Sekhetar Robots, Mutalith Vortex Beasts, Tzaangors, and Tzaangor Enlightened, this Hexwarp Thrallband list floods the board with layered, psychic-infused bodies across every role. The win condition is controlling No Man's Land objective markers to extend the Flow of Magic across the midfield, then grinding out scoring phases from behind a wall of durable infantry while Rituals on Psyker units chain into sustained healing through Ritual of Regeneration, keeping key units alive far longer than opponents budget for. It punishes attrition-based gunlines that need to chew through multiple durable units simultaneously — the sheer volume of bodies and self-repair makes trading efficiently nearly impossible. Concentrated high-AP, high-volume alpha strikes that bypass the healing loop before it activates will crack it, since the build's durability is reactive rather than upfront.
